index_test_reagent_name: Nylon brush (Cytobrush GT), liquid-based cytology with SurePath™
index_test_commercial_name: Cytobrush GT (Med-Scan Medical, Malmö, Sweden); SurePath™ (BD Diagnostics, Tripath, USA)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clearly visible oral lesions showing apparent variation from normal healthy mucosa; conspicuous oral lesions were sampled
specimen_collection: Five brush smears per lesion were taken with the nylon brush and pooled in one SurePath™ vial. The head of the brush was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times; subsequently the head was washed out thoroughly in the preservation vial.
technique: Five brush smears per lesion taken with the Cytobrush GT (nylon brush) and pooled in one SurePath™ vial. The head was placed tangentially to the lesion and rotated at least ten times, then washed out in the preservation vial. Specimens processed per SurePath™ protocol: cells deposited by gravitational force, transferred to glass slides, and stained by Papanicolaou (PAP). Evaluated using the German classification for extragenital cytology (Böcking et al.).
positivity_threshold: The results 'doubtful', 'suspicious' and 'positive' were summarized as 'tumour cell positive'. Only 'negative' was reported as 'tumour cell negative'. Negative = no malignant cells detectable; doubtful = malignant cells may be present, cannot be excluded; suspicious = urgent suspicion but malignancy not definitely detectable; positive = malignant cells clearly present.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any non-negative cytology result (doubtful, suspicious, or positive)
comments_index_test: Retrospective consecutive cohort; nylon brush arm covers January 2009–May 2012 (666 cases). Five smears per lesion were pooled in one vial, which likely influenced sensitivity/specificity compared to the single-smear rigid brush arm. The paper contains a likely typographical error in the Background section where 'nylon brush' is written for the 2012–2018 cohort, but context and Table 1 confirm this was the rigid brush period. No blinding or calibration information reported. Unit of analysis is effectively per patient/lesion (one lesion per patient sampled).

index_test_reagent_name: Rigid brush (Orcellex Brush), liquid-based cytology with SurePath™
index_test_commercial_name: Orcellex Brush (Rovers Medical Devices B.V., Oss, The Netherlands); SurePath™ (BD Diagnostics, Tripath, USA)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clearly visible oral lesions showing apparent variation of normal healthy mucosa; no restriction to specific anatomical site — any conspicuous oral lesion was eligible.
specimen_collection: One brush smear per lesion: the head of the Orcellex (rigid) brush was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times, then the head was washed out thoroughly in the SurePath™ preservation vial.
technique: The Orcellex Brush head was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times; the head was then washed out thoroughly in the SurePath™ fixation liquid vial (one obtainment per lesion). Specimens were shipped to a pathologist and processed according to SurePath™ protocol: cells deposited by gravitational force, transferred to glass slides, and stained by Papanicolaou (PAP). Cytological evaluation followed the German classification for extragenital cytology (Böcking et al.), categorising results as negative, doubtful, suspicious, or positive.
positivity_threshold: The results 'doubtful', 'suspicious' and 'positive' were summarized as 'tumour cell positive'. Only 'negative' was reported as 'tumour cell negative' for the statistical evaluation in comparison to histology.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any non-negative cytological result (doubtful, suspicious, or positive)
comments_index_test: This is a consecutive retrospective cohort study; the rigid brush arm covers June 2012 to February 2018. Each patient contributed one brush biopsy from one lesion, so patient and lesion counts are equivalent. The 8 cases excluded for insufficient sample quality (from 2026 enrolled to 2018 analyzed) are distributed across both arms; the contingency table for the rigid brush sums to exactly 1352, suggesting these 8 exclusions are already accounted for. The paper describes that the rigid brush tends to yield more 'doubtful' results than the nylon brush, which inflates false positives and reduces specificity. No calibration or blinding information is reported.

index_test_reagent_name: VELscope VX; blue excitation light wavelength 400–460 nm
site_selection_index_test: VELscope was applied to lesional and perilesional tissue of suspicious oral lesions already identified by conventional oral examination (COE). Examination followed a systematic sequence of oral soft tissue inspection per WHO (1987) guidelines.
technique: Blue excitation light (wavelength 400–460 nm) from the VELscope VX handpiece was directed at lesional and perilesional oral tissue. Tissue was assessed for visual fluorescence retention (VFR) or visual fluorescence loss (VFL) through the handpiece. Digital photographs of tissue fluorescence were acquired directly through the VELscope viewing handpiece using an iPod 5 digital camera connected by an image adapter (LED Dental Inc).
positivity_threshold: Visual fluorescence loss (VFL) when viewed through the VELscope VX handpiece is considered a positive result (test positive); visual fluorescence retention (VFR) is considered a negative result.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (VFL)
blinding_index_test_assessors: The VELscope examiner was not explicitly stated to be blinded to histopathology results. Given the sequential design (VELscope performed before biopsy), the examiner would not have had histopathology results at the time of VELscope examination. The histopathologist was blinded to DVFE findings: 'without information of the DVFE findings.'
comments_index_test: Single-arm study with one index test (VELscope). The biopsy site was chosen to cover both COE and VEL positive regions, which may create partial verification bias. The paper reports results at the lesion level (one lesion per patient, 50 total), consistent with 50 patients. The examiner performing VELscope also performed COE — no independent evaluation. The histopathologist was blinded to DVFE findings, but the VELscope examiner's blinding to clinical information is not stated. Study conducted in Iraq and described as the first such study in that country.

index_test_reagent_name: Papanicolaou stain; alcohol-based liquid fixative (BD SurePath Collection Vial)
site_selection_index_test: Specimens were collected from clearly visible oral lesions showing apparent variation from the normal healthy mucosa. Sites included the tongue, gingiva, buccal mucosa, palate, lip, and floor of the mouth — regions where SCC was most frequently observed.
specimen_collection: Cells were collected using the Orcellex® Brush by twisting the brush ten times on the lesion; the head of the cell collector was then transferred directly into an alcohol-based liquid in the BD SurePath™ Collection Vial and transported to the laboratory.
technique: Cytology performed using BD SurePath™. Cells collected with Orcellex® Brush (twisted ten times); brush head transferred into alcohol-based liquid in BD SurePath™ Collection Vial and transported to lab. Cells stained with Papanicolaou stain per standard procedure. Assessment performed using modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system, including cellularity, quality of preparation, cell types, microbiota, inflammatory cells, artifacts, and dyskeratotic/SCC features. Slides reported as inadequate if poor cellularity, poor fixation (air-dried), or thickly spread/obscured elements.
positivity_threshold: For statistical analysis, cytology was classified as negative (negative result) and positive (doubtful or positive result). 'Positive' signified malignant cells observed; 'doubtful' signified malignant cells suspected but not confirmed; 'negative' signified no atypical cells observed.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: malignant cells observed OR suspected (doubtful or positive result)
calibration_of_assessors: All participating experts had passed the board examination of the Japanese Society of Pathology for oral pathology and had been practicing for >7 years. Discrepancies in assessment were settled by consensus among at least two of five oral pathology diagnostic experts. No formal pre-study calibration exercise is described.
comments_index_test: This is a single-center, retrospective study. The 2 inadequate material cases were excluded from sensitivity/specificity calculations (n analyzed = 651). Notably, 'doubtful' results were merged with 'positive' results to form the test-positive group for statistical analysis, which likely increases sensitivity but inflates false-positive rate. This dichotomization decision should be considered when comparing with other studies. The study has only one index test arm (LBC), so no multi-arm independence concerns.

index_test_reagent_name: Multispectral autofluorescence endoscopy system, 355 nm pulsed laser excitation, emission at 390 ± 20 nm, 452 ± 22.5 nm, and >500 nm spectral bands
site_selection_index_test: Imaging was performed on clinically suspicious oral lesions identified by an experienced head and neck surgeon during clinical examination, as well as a clinically healthy-appearing area on the corresponding contralateral anatomical side.
technique: A 355 nm pulsed laser (~1 ns pulse width, ~1 μJ/pulse at tissue) was used to excite tissue autofluorescence. Emission was collected at 390±20 nm, 452±22.5 nm, and >500 nm spectral bands, corresponding to collagen, NADH, and FAD autofluorescence. Images were acquired with a 10 mm circular field-of-view, ~100 μm lateral resolution, and <3 s acquisition time per multispectral image. Total energy delivered was 2.8 mJ. Images were acquired from both the suspicious oral lesion and the contralateral healthy-appearing area. Preprocessing included background subtraction, saturation masking, 5×5 spatial averaging, SNR masking (<15 dB), and manual masking of teeth regions. Autofluorescence intensity features were computed per pixel and used to train and apply an L1-SVM classifier, yielding a posterior probability map; the image-level score (mean of map) was compared to an optimized threshold for classification.
positivity_threshold: The validation sample was classified as cancer/precancer if its predicted image-level score (average of the posterior probability map) was greater than or equal to the optimized threshold (selected from ROC curve as the point with maximum sensitivity within the 1-specificity range of 0% to 30%), or as benign otherwise.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: image-level score ≥ ROC-optimized threshold (max sensitivity at 1-specificity 0–30%)
blinding_index_test_assessors: The tissue biopsy (reference standard) was blinded to the autofluorescence endoscopy imaging acquisition and processing. In the LOPOCV, each validation sample was blinded to model training, suggesting the classification system was not informed by histopathology results during image-level prediction.
comments_index_test: This is a single-arm study with one index test (multispectral autofluorescence endoscopy). A secondary comparison is made against a simulated VELscope model (single-feature SVM using I452,n + I500,n), but this is a computational simulation not a separate device arm. Classification is automated (ML-based) rather than clinician-read, which is atypical for diagnostic accuracy studies and has implications for risk-of-bias assessment. The LOPOCV strategy with only 67 patients and class imbalance (34 benign vs 33 cancer/precancer) may produce optimistic performance estimates. The optimized threshold was derived from the training set within each LOPOCV fold, which is methodologically sound but should be noted. Unit of analysis is lesions (one per patient), so patient- and lesion-level counts are equivalent here.

index_test_reagent_name: Single-feature model simulating VELscope: combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at 452 ± 22.5 nm and >500 nm emission bands (I452,n + I500,n)
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspicious oral lesions and a clinically healthy-appearing area in the corresponding contralateral anatomical side, selected by an experienced head and neck surgeon; same site-selection as the multispectral arm (shared imaging dataset).
technique: A linear L1-SVM model (C=1) was trained using a single spectral feature consisting of the combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at the 452 ± 22.5 nm and >500 nm emission bands (I452,n + I500,n), simulating the VELscope autofluorescence emission. The model was trained and cross-validated using the same LOPOCV strategy as the multispectral model. Image-level classification followed the same pipeline: pixel-level posterior probability map → image-level average score → comparison against optimized ROC threshold.
positivity_threshold: The validation sample was classified as cancer/precancer if its predicted image-level score (average of pixel-level posterior probability map) was greater than or equal to the optimized threshold selected from ROC analysis of the training set (point on ROC curve with maximum sensitivity within 1-specificity range of 0% to 30%).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: image-level average posterior probability score ≥ optimized ROC threshold
blinding_index_test_assessors: The index test (automated computational model) was blinded to histopathology by design: the validation sample image was excluded from training at each LOPOCV fold, and biopsy results were not used in model prediction. The tissue biopsy examiner was also explicitly stated to be blinded to autofluorescence imaging.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the index test is a fully automated algorithm; no human examiner interprets the index test result, so blinding to clinical information is not applicable in the traditional sense. The paper does not explicitly address blinding of the algorithmic model to patient clinical information.
comments_index_test: This arm is not an independent test but a computational simulation of the VELscope system using a single spectral feature (I452,n + I500,n) extracted from the same multispectral autofluorescence images acquired for the primary arm. Both arms share the same 67 patients/lesions, so they are not independent and meta-analytic pooling should account for this overlap. The VELscope simulation is imperfect: the actual VELscope uses 400–460 nm blue-light excitation, whereas this model uses 355 nm pulsed laser excitation with NADH (452 nm) and FAD (>500 nm) emission bands. Results: sensitivity 61%, specificity 71%, accuracy 66%.

site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied to clinically visible oral lesions identified by the consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon. All patients with clinically visible oral cavity lesions were included; the stain was applied directly to the lesion.
technique: Patients rinsed their mouth with water, then used 1% acetic acid mouthwash for 20 seconds. Then 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion with a cotton swab, followed by 1% acetic acid mouthwash to remove excess stain. Staining was recorded as positive or negative irrespective of intensity.
positivity_threshold: The staining is recorded as positive or negative irrespective of the intensity of the stain.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any stain retention (irrespective of intensity)
comments_index_test: 1. The same consultant performed both clinical examination and TB application/interpretation, meaning TB results were not independent of clinical findings — high risk of bias for index test interpretation. 2. The biopsy (reference standard) was taken from the TB-stained site, introducing potential partial verification bias (non-stained lesions had biopsy site decided clinically). 3. Staining positivity defined as any retention regardless of intensity — no graded or intensity-based threshold. 4. A secondary analysis excluding cases with epithelial hyperplasia and heavy inflammation was performed to address false positives; these results (sensitivity 100%, specificity 60% for TB) are also reported in the Discussion. 5. Sub-analysis of 15 patients with prior surgery/radiotherapy is reported separately in Tables 5–6.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the clinically identified oral lesion (persistent >3 weeks), covering approximately 2 cm margin all around the lesion
technique: 1% Toluidine Blue solution prepared from 1 g TB dye powder, 10 ml 1% acetic acid, 4.19 ml absolute alcohol, and 86 ml distilled water. Procedure: (1) mouth rinsed with water to remove debris; (2) 1% acetic acid rinse for 20 s to remove saliva; (3) area dried with gauze; (4) dye applied over the oral lesion with a cotton swab, gently, for 1 min, covering ~2 cm margin all around the lesion; (5) 1% acetic acid rinse for 1 min; (6) dye uptake pattern observed under proper light and exposure. Biopsy taken from the area of maximum stain retention.
positivity_threshold: A stain was considered as positive for malignancy if the lesion diffusely or partly stained dark blue (royal or navy blue), or had stippled appearance. All equivocal lesions were considered positively stained unless proved otherwise.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: diffuse or partial dark blue (royal/navy) stain retention or stippled appearance; equivocal counted as positive
blinding_index_test_assessors: NR — not explicitly stated whether the clinician interpreting the TB staining result was blinded to the reference standard (histopathology). The pathologists were blinded to the staining result, but blinding of TB assessors to histopathology is not reported.
comments_index_test: This study uses TB staining as a biopsy site-selection guide rather than a standalone screening test. The TB result (positive/negative) is compared against histopathology as the reference standard. Group allocation was by alternate sampling (not true randomisation), which is a methodological limitation acknowledged by the authors. The study is a two-arm comparison (Group A: clinical judgment biopsy vs Group B: TB-guided biopsy), both proceeding to wedge biopsy and histopathology. The TB positivity threshold includes equivocal lesions as positive, which may inflate sensitivity and reduce specificity. The 2×2 table for Group B yields: TP=58, FP=7, FN=3, TN=32 (total=100 patients).

site_selection_index_test: Whole-mouth rinse applied to all patients presenting with oral lesions (buccal mucosa, lateral border of tongue, retromolar trigone, and other oral sites) identified during comprehensive head and neck examination.
technique: Mouth rinsed with water for 20 s to remove debris; 1% acetic acid rinse for 20 s to remove ropey saliva; 1% toluidine blue oral rinse for 20 s; second 1% acetic acid rinse to remove mechanically retained stain; final water rinse.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that exhibited dark blue staining were deemed positive for premalignant or malignant tissue, while those with light staining or no color were considered negative and were scheduled for follow-up.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention
comments_index_test: Single-arm study (toluidine blue only); no comparator index test. Authors note the study is hospital-based and results may not generalise to primary care settings. Tables 4 and 5 show identical 2×2 cell counts for TB staining vs clinical examination and TB staining vs histopathology (71 TP, 3 FP, 17 FN, 9 TN), suggesting near-complete concordance between clinical and histopathological diagnoses — this limits independent evaluation of the index test. The figure label shows 0.1% toluidine blue solution bottle, but the text consistently refers to 1% solution; this discrepancy should be noted. Cohen's kappa = 0.370 (fair agreement).

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically identified oral PMD lesions (white or red and white lesions suspicious of PMD) that were pre-identified during clinical examination
technique: Patients rinsed mouths with clean water; lesions were dried with gauze and photographed. 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds. A photograph was taken after application and the lesion was observed for colour changes.
positivity_threshold: The results of the acetic acid application were considered positive if the lesion appears opaque white (acetowhite) and a negative if the lesion does not show any color change.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: acetowhite (opaque white colour change)
comments_index_test: Sequential design: acetic acid was applied first, then toluidine blue was applied to the same lesion after acetic acid (acetic acid was also used as the decolorizer in the TB protocol). All 31 patients received both tests on the same lesion visit. Biopsy site selection was influenced by both clinical appearance AND dye retention, potentially introducing verification bias. Single examiner performed all index test applications and interpretations without reported blinding.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically identified oral PMD lesions (white or red and white lesions suspicious of PMD) identified during clinical examination
technique: After acetic acid application, 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds and then decolorized with acetic acid. A photograph of the lesion was taken following this procedure.
positivity_threshold: The lesion was considered toluidine blue positive if it retained blue color after the staining. Lesions with no uptake or questionable uptake constituted the negative toluidine blue category of lesions.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: blue color retention after decolorization; questionable uptake classified as negative
calibration_of_assessors: The principal investigator was trained in the specialty of oral medicine; clinical diagnoses were confirmed by an oral medicine specialist with more than 10 years' experience. No specific pre-study calibration exercise for TB stain interpretation is described.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded; a single examiner performed all observations and had full access to clinical information. The paper notes this as a limitation: 'The subjectivity in visual examination was not investigated as a single examiner performed all the observations.'
comments_index_test: Sequential application design: acetic acid was applied first, then toluidine blue was applied and decolorized with acetic acid. The two arms are not independent — prior acetic acid application may affect TB uptake/interpretation. Additionally, biopsy site selection was partly guided by TB dye retention ('The site of the biopsy was selected based on the clinical appearance and dye retention'), introducing partial verification bias for the TB arm. Questionable TB uptake was classified as negative, which improves specificity — important for cross-study comparison.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (2% Toluidine Blue Electrospun Fiber)
index_test_reagent_name: 2% toluidine blue in polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) electrospun nanofibers
site_selection_index_test: The TB electrospun fiber patch was applied directly to clinically identified suspected OPMD lesions and non-healing ulcers (persisting >2 weeks without identifiable cause). Lesion sites included buccal mucosa, alveolar ridge, lateral tongue, and buccal vestibule.
technique: First, 1% acetic acid was applied with a cotton tip to the lesion for 20 s to eliminate residue layers. Next, a 2×2 cm electrospun fiber patch containing 2% TB was applied to the lesion for 20 s. Finally, the mechanically retained stain was removed by applying 1% acetic acid with a cotton tip for 20 s. One oral medicine dentist then measured the color and intensity of the staining. When a lesion was >2 cm, multiple TB electrospun fiber patches were placed adjacent to each other to cover the affected area.
positivity_threshold: Lesions showing dark blue staining were classified as positive. Lesions showing pale/no staining were classified as negative. 'Our study only considered lesions staining dark blue as true positives.'
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not explicitly stated; however, since biopsy (reference standard) was performed after TB staining, the oral medicine dentist interpreting the staining results had not yet received histopathological results at the time of assessment. No formal blinding statement is provided.
comments_index_test: Single-arm study with only one index test (TB electrospun fiber). All 36 lesions underwent biopsy regardless of TB staining result, providing complete verification. The study did not compare TB electrospun fibers to standard TB application (e.g., solution rinse or cotton bud application), which limits conclusions about superiority of the novel delivery form. The unit of analysis is lesions (36 lesions from 30 patients), so lesion-level results do not account for clustering within patients. Pale/light blue staining was classified as negative (rather than positive), which is a more conservative threshold than some prior studies — this choice likely affected the reported specificity (35.7%).

index_test_reagent_name: Beta-defensin Index (BDI): ratio of hBD-3/hBD-2 measured by sandwich ELISA from cytobrush cell lysates
index_test_commercial_name: Phoenix Pharmaceuticals ELISA kits (Cat#EK-072-52 for hBD-2; Cat#EK-072-38 for hBD-3) for external validation; Peprotech antibody pairs for discovery/internal validation
site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush applied to the visible suspicious oral lesion and to the contralateral normal (mirror) site of the same patient. Lesions must be accessible to cytobrushing.
specimen_collection: Cytobrush samples collected from the suspicious lesion and contralateral normal site using the Rovers Orcellex Brush (Rovers Medical Devices). The clinician applied the cytobrush with pressure and turned the brush head 10 turns to collect as much of the entire thickness of the lesion as possible. The brush was then inserted into a sample collection tube containing 2 mL PBS and placed on ice. Samples stored at -80°C until ELISA.
technique: Paired cytobrush samples (lesion and contralateral normal) processed as follows: cells dislodged from brush by flicking/vortexing collection tube; centrifuged at 300×g for 5 min, supernatant discarded; cell pellet lysed in 200 µL RIPA buffer, centrifuged at 10,000×g at 4°C for 10 min; resultant supernatant (cell lysates) used for ELISA. Sandwich ELISA: 96-well plates coated with anti-hBD-2 or anti-hBD-3 antibodies (1 µg/mL, overnight 4°C); blocked with 1% BSA/PBS; 20 µL cell lysate + 80 µL RIPA added per well (duplicate); incubated 1 h RT; washed 3× PBS-Tween 0.1%; biotinylated secondary antibody (0.1 µg/mL, 30 min RT); streptavidin-peroxidase (1:200, 20 min RT); TMB substrate (Reagent A+B 1:1, 20 min); stopped with 2N HCl; OD measured at 450 nm. BDI = [OD_hBD-3/OD_hBD-2]_Lesion / [OD_hBD-3/OD_hBD-2]_Normal. External validation cohorts used Phoenix Pharmaceuticals ELISA kits per vendor instructions.
positivity_threshold: BDI ≥ 1.25 indicates cancer (cutoff value of 1.25 for cancer diagnosis, derived from discovery-phase ROC analysis yielding 100% sensitivity and 80% specificity)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: BDI ≥ 1.25 (ratio of lesion hBD-3/hBD-2 to contralateral hBD-3/hBD-2)
blinding_index_test_assessors: BDI assessors were blinded to pathology results. 'The samples were intentionally blinded so that pathologist-determined diagnoses were revealed only after BDI scores were obtained for all patients.' This applied to both discovery and validation phases.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — no statement about whether the clinician collecting the cytobrush samples was blinded to patient clinical information (history, demographics, prior diagnoses). The study describes blinding of laboratory operators to pathology diagnoses, but does not address blinding of the sample-collecting clinician to clinical information.
comments_index_test: 1. The BDI is a within-patient normalized index (lesion/contralateral ratio), making each patient their own control — this design feature reduces confounding from inter-individual variation. 2. There is an apparent arithmetic inconsistency in Table 1: TP(54)+TN(38)+FP(8)+FN(1)=101, yet n=92 is stated; the source of this discrepancy (possibly overlapping proof-of-concept subjects, or a reporting error) is not explained in the paper. 3. For external validation cohorts, a different commercial ELISA kit was used (Phoenix Pharmaceuticals) vs. in-house Peprotech antibody pairs for discovery/internal validation — potential for inter-assay variability, though the authors assert comparable results. 4. The BDI cutoff of 1.25 was derived from a single-center discovery cohort and applied to multi-center validation — as acknowledged by the authors in limitations, this may not account for demographic or site variation. 5. The 8 proof-of-concept patients (4 OSCC, 4 benign) are not included in the n=92 diagnostic accuracy analysis and their BDI data appear separately (Figure 3B/Table S1A).

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious lesions within the oral cavity (targeted application to suspicious areas, not whole-mouth rinse). Sites included buccal mucosa, tongue, gums, floor of mouth, and lip.
technique: 1. Clinically suspicious lesions photographed; lesion areas pre-treated with 1% acetic acid applied via cotton bud for 20 seconds, repeated once, then rinsed with water. 2. Toluidine blue applied with cotton bud for 10–20 seconds. 3. Lesion decolorized with 2% acetic acid via cotton bud for 20–30 seconds; photograph taken.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue was considered as positive for lesions suspicious of malignancy, light blue retention was considered as positive for premalignant lesions unless proved otherwise by biopsy, and lesion without retention was considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any dye retention (dark or light blue); negative: no retention
comments_index_test: Single-arm study with one index test (toluidine blue). Positivity threshold combines two levels (dark blue = malignancy, light blue = premalignant) both coded as 'positive' in the 2x2 table, so the threshold effectively collapses both staining intensities into a single positive category vs. no retention. The biopsy was obtained from all 100 patients prior to or following TB staining ('After obtaining Informed consent from every subject to perform a biopsy prior to application of toluidine blue stain'), which is the correct sequence for a diagnostic accuracy study but warrants noting. No waiting period for inflammatory lesion resolution was applied (unlike Mashberg's methodology), which the authors acknowledge as a source of false positives.

site_selection_index_test: The main site of morphologically altered mucosa was selected clinically and TB staining was applied to that site. As per the flow chart: 'Selection of morphologically altered mucosal site clinically using TB staining'.
technique: 1% TB applied in 4 steps: (1) rinse oral cavity with water for 20 s to remove debris; (2) application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s; (3) application or rinse with 1% TB solution (1% W/W) for 20 s; (4) application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s to eliminate mechanically retained stains. Staining was then photographed.
positivity_threshold: A royal blue or a navy blue stain was considered as a positive result even if either the entire lesion or a portion of the lesion is stained or stippled. A light blue staining is considered doubtful. If there is no colour absorbed by the lesion, it was taken as a negative stain.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: royal blue or navy blue stain retention (whole or partial lesion)
calibration_of_assessors: Dental surgeons at the selected institutions were trained by an expert in Oral Medicine at their institutions. Live demonstrations of TB application were carried out to familiarise the procedure during the training programme.
comments_index_test: 1. Five patients received TB test but were excluded from validity analysis due to missing histopathological data (65 received vs. 60 analyzed). 2. Verification bias risk: TB-positive cases had biopsies taken from the TB-positive site, while TB-negative cases had biopsies from the clinically selected site — this differential biopsy site selection could affect sensitivity/specificity estimates. 3. 'Doubtful' (light blue) cases are not clearly classified as positive or negative in the analysis; their handling is not reported. 4. No control group (acknowledged as limitation by authors). 5. Multi-centre study (3 sites); inter-site consistency of TB application not formally assessed beyond training.

index_test_reagent_name: toluidine blue (1% acetic acid used for pre-cleaning)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinician-identified suspected lesions (precancerous lesions or oral squamous cell carcinoma) after an oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings and picked the areas to be examined. Biopsy subsequently performed at the blue-stained area.
technique: A cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid was used to clean the lesion prior to the application of toluidine blue with a different cotton tip for 30 s. Subsequently, a third cotton bud soaked with 1% acetic acid was used to remove any excess toluidine blue on the lesion. The patient then rinsed out their mouth.
positivity_threshold: A positive lesion was the one which color changed to blue, while a negative lesion was with no change.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: blue colour change (stain retention)
comments_index_test: The TB arm includes two patient groups: 33 patients who received TB only and 24 patients who received both TB and vinegar. The combined TB analysis in Table 2 covers 67 specimens from 54 patients, but 33+24=57 patients received TB — the discrepancy (54 vs 57) is unexplained. The 24 patients who received both substances were excluded from the immunohistochemical (p53) analysis. The paper notes a distinction between 'dark royal blue' (true positive) and 'pale blue' (false positive) staining but did not apply this distinction to the positivity threshold prospectively, which may inflate false positives and lower specificity.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinician-identified suspected lesion areas. 'An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.' Vinegar was applied to the specific lesion selected by the specialist.
technique: A gauze soaked with vinegar was applied to a clean and dry lesion for one minute. The researcher noted the changes and photographed the lesion. An incisional biopsy was performed at the area that had turned opaque white. If the lesion did not change colour, a biopsy was performed at the central area of the lesion.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was designated when a lesion changed to opaque white. When a lesion did not change or changed to transparent white, a negative finding was indicated.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: lesion changes to opaque white
comments_index_test: There is a numerical discrepancy: the Methods section states 30 patients received vinegar-only and 24 received both vinegar and toluidine blue (total 54 patients with vinegar), but Table 3 reports 83 specimens from 57 patients. This 3-patient discrepancy is unexplained and should be noted as a potential reporting error. Additionally, the 24 patients who received both substances are included in Table 3 (vinegar sensitivity/specificity) but are excluded from the immunohistochemical (Ki67) analysis, meaning the sensitivity/specificity data and the Ki67 correlation data derive from overlapping but non-identical patient sets. This should be considered in meta-analysis when combining diagnostic accuracy and biomarker data.

site_selection_index_test: Suspected oral squamous cell carcinoma lesions identified clinically; an oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
specimen_collection: Incisional biopsy performed at the area that turned opaque white and had stained blue. If the areas that had stained blue and turned opaque white were not coincident, incisional biopsies were performed at both areas. If the lesion did not stain or change color, a biopsy was performed at the central area of the lesion.
technique: Vinegar (5% acetic acid) was applied first, followed by toluidine blue application. Vinegar was applied using a gauze soaked with vinegar on a clean and dry lesion for one minute; changes were noted and photographed. Then toluidine blue was applied: lesion cleaned with cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid, toluidine blue applied with a cotton tip for 30 s, excess removed with a third cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid, and the patient rinsed out their mouth. Photographs were taken of the combined result.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was indicated for a lesion with color changed to both opaque white and blue, while a negative finding was a lesion not demonstrating these combined changes.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: lesion changed to both opaque white (acetic acid) and blue (toluidine blue)
comments_index_test: The 24 patients in the combined arm were excluded from immunohistochemical analysis (p53 and Ki67), so no IHC correlation data are available for this arm. Sensitivity/specificity analysis is based on 28 lesions from 24 patients. Note: the Results section text states '27 lesions' were tested with both substances but Table 4 header states '28 specimens from 24 patients' — minor discrepancy in the paper. Lesion counts from Table 4 (28 total) used here as the more precise figure.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious oral cavity lesions identified during standard examination; sites included buccal mucosa, tongue, gingivo-buccal sulcus, alveolus, floor of mouth, retromolar trigone, and lip.
technique: Clinically suspicious oral cavity lesions were stained with toluidine blue dye. Lesions that showed dark blue staining were considered positive; those with light staining or no staining were considered negative. Detailed procedural steps (concentration, pre-rinse, dwell time, wash-off) are not described.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that showed dark blue staining were considered to be positive for premalignant or malignant tissue, while those with light staining, or totally not coloured, were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention; negative: light or no staining
comments_index_test: 1) The full toluidine blue protocol (concentration, acetic acid pre-rinse, dwell time, wash steps) is not described — limits reproducibility assessment. 2) Both NBI and TB were administered to the same 44 patients, so the two arms are not independent; this should be accounted for in meta-analysis. 3) The paper reports sensitivity/specificity separately for premalignant and malignant lesion detection, yielding different values in the abstract vs. Discussion (premalignant: 66.6%/87.8%; malignant: 94.3%/100%) — reviewers should select the appropriate outcome stratum. 4) Light staining was categorised as negative/inconclusive, which affects sensitivity calculations.

index_test_reagent_name: Narrow Band Imaging (NBI) — no chemical reagent; optical filter-based endoscopic imaging system
site_selection_index_test: NBI was applied to clinically suspicious oral cavity lesions identified during standard clinical examination. Sites examined included buccal mucosa, tongue, gingivo-buccal sulcus, alveolus, floor of mouth, retromolar trigone, and lip. Patients first underwent zero-degree endoscopic examination in white light, followed by NBI of the suspicious lesion areas.
technique: Patients underwent zero-degree endoscopic examination first in white light, then NBI mode was activated. NBI uses optical filters narrowing white light to 400–430 nm (blue, centred at 415 nm) and 525–555 nm (green, centred at 540 nm). The 415 nm light enhances superficial capillaries (IPCLs, displayed as brown dots); the 540 nm light highlights deeper submucosal vessels (displayed as cyan). Images were captured and assessed using Kamath et al. classification: normal mucosa shows clear branching vessels; neoplastic lesions show scattered brown spots (IPCLs) with altered vascularity, irregular borders, weaving pattern, and loss of normal branching. Photographs of the suspected area were taken.
positivity_threshold: Altered or hyper vascularity and increased capillaries (brown dots/IPCLs) suggestive of malignancy; lesions with irregular borders, weaving pattern, irregular and increased vascularity with increased capillary loops (IPCLs) were considered positive/malignant. Normal/uniform vascularity was considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: altered/hyper vascularity with increased IPCLs (brown dots)
comments_index_test: This is a paired two-arm study where all 44 patients received both NBI and toluidine blue; arms are not independent. Sensitivity/specificity are reported separately for malignant and premalignant lesion subgroups. For malignant lesions: sensitivity 100%, specificity 88.8%; for premalignant lesions: sensitivity 66.6%, specificity 95%. NBI classification followed Kamath et al. criteria. Small sample size (n=44) limits generalisability. Patients with proven malignancy were excluded at enrolment, which may affect spectrum and prevalence estimates.

site_selection_index_test: Applied directly to the oral leukoplakia lesion on the buccal mucosa (all patients had lesions on buccal mucosa); the target lesional area was selected for staining.
technique: Patients rinsed mouth with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds to remove food debris. Mucosa of the target area was dried with gauze. 1% MB dye was applied directly on the lesion with a cotton bud for 30 seconds. Patients then rinsed with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds to wash out excess dye. Pattern of dye retention was assessed by intensity of stain retention.
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue/deep blue stains of MB were considered as positive retention. Wide, shallow, faint, pale royal blue stains or no retention of the stain were considered as negative for MB retention.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark royal blue/deep blue stain retention
calibration_of_assessors: Two examiners (DS, AK) independently interpreted staining in all cases; disagreements were resolved by a third examiner (AS) with majority opinion. Disagreement occurred in only 2 of 50 cases. No formal pre-study calibration or training exercise is described.
comments_index_test: Important discrepancy: the abstract states '5% MB' was used, while the Methods section states '1% MB dye was applied.' The methods section is more detailed and likely authoritative, but this inconsistency should be flagged for risk-of-bias assessment. Additionally, all 50 patients received both MB alone and the MB+LI double staining sequentially — the two arms are not independent; the same patients contributed to both arms. This within-patient design means the two test results are correlated and the arms share the same reference standard biopsy.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (Methylene Blue + Lugol's Iodine Double Staining)
index_test_reagent_name: 1% methylene blue followed by 3% Lugol's iodine
site_selection_index_test: Applied to the oral leukoplakia lesion on buccal mucosa (lesional and perilesional sites). All patients had lesions on buccal mucosa. MB was applied directly on the lesion; LI was subsequently applied to the lesional and perilesional sites.
technique: Patients rinsed with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds to remove food debris; mucosa of the target area was dried with gauze. 1% MB dye was applied directly on the lesion with a cotton bud for 30 seconds; patients then rinsed with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds to wash out excess dye. Subsequently, 3% LI was applied to the lesional and perilesional sites with a cotton bud for 10–20 seconds.
positivity_threshold: For double staining: MB positive (dark royal blue/deep blue) AND LI negative (pale yellow or unstained) = positive for dysplasia. MB negative (pale blue/no retention) AND LI negative (pale yellow or unstained) = also positive for dysplasia. MB negative AND LI positive (dark brown staining) = negative (normal/hyperkeratosis). In effect, LI negativity (pale yellow or unstained areas) indicates dysplasia regardless of MB result.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LI unstained/pale yellow (regardless of MB result); negative: LI dark brown staining
calibration_of_assessors: Stain interpretation was conducted by two examiners (DS, AK) in all cases. In case of disagreement, a third examiner (AS) evaluated the lesion and the decision was taken in favour of majority opinion. Out of 50 cases, there was disagreement in only 2 cases, resolved by the third examiner.
comments_index_test: The double staining arm uses MB followed by LI in sequence on the same patient/lesion, making it a combined/sequential test rather than two independent arms. The paper notes a practical difficulty: in lesions retaining MB, subsequent LI application produces a mixed colour that may be difficult to distinguish from mahogany (LI-positive), introducing potential interpretive ambiguity. The operative positivity criterion for the double staining method is effectively LI negativity — MB result alone does not determine the double-staining outcome. All 50 patients had lesions exclusively on buccal mucosa, limiting generalisability. Study is cross-sectional with no control group of normal mucosa.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to all lesions clinically diagnosed as OPMDs during oral examination. Conventional oral examination was first performed under incandescent light, then the Identafi® white light was used to visualize the extent of each lesion, followed by violet light examination of the same lesion area.
technique: Room and operatory lights were dimmed. White light of Identafi® was used to visualize the extent of the lesion. The instrument was then switched to violet light (405 nm) to examine for loss of autofluorescence (LOA); suspicious lesions appear dark. All lesions displaying LOA were blanched to evaluate diascopic fluorescence. Loss of autofluorescence (LOA) and presence of blanching were noted.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that displayed LOA were considered to be positive and lesions that displayed no LOA or gain of autofluorescence were considered to be negative. Further, on blanching, the lesions that achieved complete blanching were considered negative and lesions with partial blanching were considered to be positive for LOA.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (LOA) or partial blanching on diascopy
comments_index_test: The unit of analysis is lesions (n=63 from 49 patients), meaning multiple lesions per patient were included and analyzed independently — this may violate independence assumptions. The study includes only OPMDs with mild and moderate dysplasia (no severe dysplasia or OSCC), limiting generalizability. All three arms (violet light, green-amber light, toluidine blue) were applied sequentially to all 63 lesions, so arms are not independent. The biopsy site was selected based on a combination of LOA, TB positivity, and clinical judgement, which may introduce verification bias. The p-value for violet light (p=0.097) was not significant at 5% level; authors note significance only at 10% level.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to all clinically identified OPMD lesions during sequential oral cavity examination; the instrument was switched to green-amber light after white light and violet light examination of the same lesions.
technique: Room and operatory lights were dimmed. After white light and violet light examination, the Identafi® was switched to green-amber light (545 nm wavelength). The examiner directly observed the vasculature (arrangement of blood vessels) of abnormal tissue compared with normal surrounding tissue. Diffuseness of vasculature was noted.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with diffuse vascularity (appeared darker) were considered to be positive and lesions without visible vasculature or with vasculature similar to the surrounding mucosa were considered to be negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: diffuse vascularity (darker appearance under green-amber light)
comments_index_test: The green-amber light arm shares all 63 lesions and 49 patients with the violet light arm (both are Identafi® sequential examinations performed on the same lesions in the same session). Arms are not independent; same examiner applied both. The unit of analysis is lesions (63), not patients (49). Sensitivity 78.4%, specificity only 15.4% — very low specificity, p=0.389 (non-significant). Keratotic lesions may have artifactually increased false positives (lesions with keratotic features appeared more prominent under green-amber light).

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically identified OPMD lesions; toluidine blue staining was performed on the same lesion sites identified during clinical oral examination and Identafi® screening
technique: Toluidine blue prepared as described by Mashberg. Patients rinsed mouth with water for 20 s to remove debris. Then 1% acetic acid was applied for 20 s to remove rosy saliva. The area was gently dried with gauze. Then 1% toluidine blue solution was applied to the lesion with cotton swab for 1 min. After that 1% acetic acid was applied for one minute. Finally, patients were asked to rinse with water again.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue stain uptake was considered positive. A light blue staining or absence of staining was taken as a negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain uptake/retention
comments_index_test: Unit of analysis is lesions (n=63) not patients (n=49); multiple lesions per patient included. Toluidine blue was applied sequentially after Identafi® screening by the same examiner, meaning the TB assessor was not blinded to prior Identafi® findings — potential for carry-over bias. Reference standard (biopsy site) was selected using combined information from Identafi® LOA, TB staining, and clinical judgment, which may introduce partial verification bias. No severe dysplasia cases were included; only mild and moderate dysplasia, which may explain the relatively low sensitivity (51.4%) given TB's known poor performance for mild/moderate dysplasia.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically identified suspicious oral leukoplakia lesions
technique: TBS (1%) was applied to the suspected oral leukoplakia lesions on the day following AA and LIS application. Pre- and post-staining images were taken. To reduce false positives, all lesions staining positive were re-stained after 2 weeks. Detailed procedural steps (rinse, dwell time, wash) are not described.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
calibration_of_assessors: Standardisation across all examiners was described but no specific training or calibration procedure is detailed.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were used for screening/recruitment and stain application to prevent bias, but blinding to clinical information is not explicitly stated.
comments_index_test: 1) All three stains (AA, LIS, TBS) were applied to the same 45 patients, making this a within-subject multi-arm design; TBS was applied on day 2. 2) Table 2 denominators for TBS (TP+FN+FP+TN = 20+3+8+3 = 34) do not sum to 45 enrolled patients — the discrepancy is unexplained and raises concerns about which patients/lesions are included in the analysis. 3) Sensitivity (91.59%) and specificity (23.33%) figures should be interpreted cautiously given this unexplained denominator issue. 4) Control group consisted of patients with epithelial hyperplasia (histopathology), not truly disease-free individuals.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspected oral leukoplakia lesions identified during initial screening
technique: Lugol's iodine (3% dilution) was applied to suspected oral leukoplakia lesions on day 1 (same day as acetic acid). Pre- and post-staining images were taken. All lesions that stained positive were re-stained after 2 weeks to reduce false-positive rates. No further procedural detail (dwell time, rinse steps) is described.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
calibration_of_assessors: Standardisation across examiners was described but no formal calibration exercise is reported: 'The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.'
comments_index_test: 1) Table 2 totals (TP+FN+FP+TN = 20+3+9+2 = 34) are inconsistent with the 45 enrolled patients — the paper does not explain this discrepancy, and the true analyzed N is unclear. 2) No positivity criterion for LIS is defined in the Methods. 3) Specificity is very low (12.22%), attributed by authors to reduced glycogen in the hyperplasia control group causing false positives. 4) LIS and AA were applied on day 1; toluidine blue on day 2 — sequence effects not discussed. 5) Positive results were re-stained at 2 weeks, but it is unclear whether the re-stain result or the original result was used in the 2×2 table.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically identified suspected oral leukoplakia lesions in the oral cavity
technique: On the first day, each patient received AA (acetic acid) solution application to their suspected lesions. Pre- and post-staining images were taken to analyse the stains. Positive results at initial application were re-stained after 2 weeks to lower the false positive rate. No further step-by-step protocol (dwell time, rinse steps) is described.
positivity_threshold: Acetowhite appearance indicating dysplasia when acetic acid is applied
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: acetowhite appearance
calibration_of_assessors: Identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study; different examiners were involved in screening/recruiting and stain application to prevent bias. No further calibration detail provided.
comments_index_test: All three index tests (AA, LIS, TBS) were applied to the same 45 patients (AA and LIS on day 1, TBS on day 2), meaning the arms are not independent — the same lesions received all three tests. The acetic acid application protocol is poorly described (no dwell time, wash steps, or concentration confirmation beyond '2%'). Sensitivity of 58.25% and specificity of 34.44% are notably lower than TBS and LIS. The control group consists of epithelial hyperplasia cases rather than normal mucosa, which may affect specificity calculations. Results presented as percentages in Table 2 but underlying counts can be back-calculated (TP=13, FN=10, FP=7, TN=4 of 34 dysplastic and 11 hyperplasia cases implied).

index_test_reagent_name: Oral liquid-based brush cytology using Orcellex brush with ThinPrep preparation
index_test_commercial_name: Orcellex brush (Rovers Medical Devices); ThinPrep PreservCyt (Hologic Inc.); ThinPrep 2000 processor (Hologic Inc.)
site_selection_index_test: Brush samples were obtained from clinically visible lesions (oral leukoplakia or OSCC) at their presenting sites, including lateral tongue, floor of mouth, labial/buccal mucosa, and alveolar ridge/palate. The brush was applied directly to the clinically diagnosed lesion.
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy performed using Orcellex® brush under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsies. Samples preserved in methanol-based preservative vials (ThinPrep® PreservCyt, Hologic Inc.).
technique: Oral brush biopsy using Orcellex® brush performed under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsies. Samples preserved in ThinPrep® PreservCyt methanol-based vials and transported to the laboratory. Liquid-based cytology slides prepared using ThinPrep® 2000 processor (Hologic Inc.) per manufacturer's instructions. Slides stained with Papanicolaou stain. Cytological assessment performed using the modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system, classifying cases as: atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, or OSCC.
positivity_threshold: Cases classified using the modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system with OLBC grading scores: 12 = no dysplasia, 9 = low-grade SIL, 6 = high-grade SIL, 3 = OSCC. Cut-off values for each histopathological category obtained based on Youden's index from ROC coordinates.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: low-grade SIL or higher (score ≤9); graded ordinal scale (modified Bethesda: undetermined significance, low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, OSCC)
comments_index_test: The OLBC slides were prepared from samples originally collected for prior studies; 34.5% of cell blocks were excluded due to inadequate cellularity (original preservative had been used for multiple prior slides), meaning the 72 included cases are a selected subset of 110 original samples. The authors acknowledge this as a limitation. One additional patient excluded from OLBC grading analysis due to Papanicolaou staining defect (n=71 analyzed). The OLBC grading and the cell block immunocytochemistry (MMR proteins) are two separate arms assessed in the same patients — both arms share the same patient cohort (same brush specimen), so independence assumptions for meta-analysis are violated if both arms are pooled.

index_test_arm_label: Cell Block Immunocytochemistry (Cumulative MMR Protein Index)
index_test_reagent_name: Immunocytochemistry for MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, PMS-2 on FFPE cell blocks (thromboplastin-plasma method)
index_test_commercial_name: Agilent Dako antibodies (MSH-6 clone EP49, MSH-2 clone FE11, MLH-1 clone ES05, PMS-2 clone EP51)
site_selection_index_test: Brush samples were taken from clinically diagnosed OLK or OSCC lesions at various oral sites (lateral tongue, floor of mouth, labial/buccal mucosa, alveolar ridge and palate). Cell blocks for ICC were prepared from the remaining cellular material in the same OLBC vials used for cytology slides.
specimen_collection: Brush biopsy samples were collected from oral lesions using Orcellex® brushes under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsy, preserved in methanol-based preservative vials (ThinPrep® PreservCyt). After ThinPrep® slide preparation, remaining cells were processed to form FFPE cell blocks using the thromboplastin-plasma method. Cell blocks with ≥1×10⁶ cells were considered adequate.
technique: Standard ICC staining was performed on 4-μm sections of FFPE cell blocks for four proteins: MSH-6 (clone EP49), MSH-2 (clone FE11), MLH-1 (clone ES05), and PMS-2 (clone EP51), all Agilent Dako. Antibody expression was scored by multiplying staining intensity (0=none, 1=weak, 2=moderate, 3=strong) by percentage of positive cells (≤24%=1, 25–50%=2, 51–75%=3, ≥76%=4). Two independent observers assessed slides blindly, counting >500 cells at ×100 magnification in 10 random fields. The index score per protein = intensity score × positivity score. The cumulative score per case = sum of index scores of all four proteins. Cut-off values for histopathological categories were derived from ROC curve coordinates using Youden's index.
positivity_threshold: Cumulative index cut-offs derived from Youden's index on ROC: 7.76–12 = No dysplasia; 5.51–7.75 = Low-risk lesion; 2.76–5.5 = High-risk lesion; 0–2.75 = OSCC. For binary discrimination: OED absent vs. present and OSCC absent vs. present thresholds were used to calculate AUC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: cumulative MMR protein score below category-specific Youden's index cut-off (≤7.75 for any dysplasia; ≤2.75 for OSCC)
calibration_of_assessors: Three cell lines prepared as cell blocks (PE/CA-PJ15 [OSCC], DOK [dysplastic oral keratinocytes], HOK [normal oral keratinocytes]) were used for antibody optimization before study assessment.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Each slide was assessed blindly by two independent observers; however, the paper does not explicitly state whether they were blinded to the histopathological (reference standard) diagnosis.
comments_index_test: 1. The ICC (cumulative MMR index) arm shares the same cell block specimens as the OLBC cytology arm — these are not independent cohorts; both arms analyzed the same 72 patients, creating dependency that must be accounted for in meta-analysis. 2. 38/110 (34.5%) cell blocks were excluded due to inadequate cellularity because the original OLBC vials had already been used for ThinPrep slide preparation in prior studies — this introduces potential selection bias. 3. This is a retrospective study using previously accumulated samples. 4. The accuracy reported for cumulative index (75.81%) is considerably lower than OLBC cytology alone (95.07%), limiting its standalone utility. 5. The combined index (ICC + OLBC) had accuracy of 92.25%, suggesting complementary value but dependency between arms.

index_test_arm_label: Combined Index (OLBC Cytology + Cumulative MMR Immunocytochemistry)
index_test_reagent_name: Combined score of OLBC cytology grading and cumulative MMR protein immunocytochemistry (MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, PMS-2)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically diagnosed oral leukoplakia (OLK) or oral squamous cell carcinoma lesions; brush samples obtained from visible lesions before surgical biopsy
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy using Orcellex® brush (Rovers Medical Devices, the Netherlands) under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsies. Samples preserved in methanol-based preservative vials (ThinPrep® PreservCyt, Hologic Inc., MA, USA).
technique: The combined index integrates two scores: (1) OLBC cytology grading: ThinPrep® slides prepared using ThinPrep® 2000 processor, stained with Papanicolaou, classified using modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system (undetermined significance SIL=12, low-grade SIL=9, high-grade SIL=6, OSCC=3). Cell blocks also prepared using thromboplastin-plasma method, H&E stained. (2) Cumulative MMR ICC: 4-μm cell block sections stained for MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, PMS-2; each scored as intensity (0–3) × % positive cells (1–4); cumulative score = sum of four protein index scores. Combined index score = sum of OLBC grading score + cumulative MMR index score; cut-offs derived via Youden's index from ROC curve coordinates (≥8.26 = no dysplasia; 5.76–8.25 = low-grade; 3.76–5.75 = high-grade; 0–3.75 = OSCC).
positivity_threshold: Combined index score cut-offs: 8.26–12 = no dysplasia; 5.76–8.25 = low-grade lesion; 3.76–5.75 = high-grade lesion; 0–3.75 = OSCC. Cut-off values derived using Youden's index from ROC curve coordinates.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive (any dysplasia or OSCC): combined index score ≤8.25; graded further by score range
calibration_of_assessors: For ICC assessment, each slide was assessed blindly by two independent observers counting more than 500 cells at ×100 magnification in 10 random fields. For antibody optimization, three cell lines prepared as cell blocks were used: PE/CA-PJ15 (OSCC), DOK (dysplastic oral keratinocytes) and HOK (normal oral keratinocytes).
blinding_index_test_assessors: ICC slides assessed blindly by two independent observers; no explicit statement that assessors were blinded to histopathological diagnosis for either the cytology or ICC components.
comments_index_test: The combined index is a post-hoc derived composite score (OLBC cytology grading score + cumulative MMR ICC score). Cut-offs were derived from the same dataset used for evaluation (no independent validation cohort), introducing potential overfitting/optimism bias. 34.5% of cell blocks were excluded for inadequate cellularity (38/110), which may introduce selection bias. One additional patient was excluded from OLBC cytology, so the effective n for the combined index is likely 71. The combined index AUC for discriminating OED presence/absence was 0.961 and for OSCC 0.977. Study is retrospective; samples were drawn from previously collected OLBC archive, which may have reduced cellularity due to prior use for other studies.

index_test_reagent_name: Modified brush cytology using medium bristle toothbrush; smear deposited directly onto glass slide
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions. The brush was used at the lesion site; most common sites were buccal mucosa (74.07%), tongue (18.52%), hard palate, and lower alveolar region. Patients with inaccessible lesions were excluded.
specimen_collection: Material collected by scrubbing the lesion with a commercially available toothbrush (medium bristles); material deposited directly onto a glass slide.
technique: Patients rinsed oral cavity with normal saline before the procedure. A commercially available medium-bristle toothbrush was used to scrub the lesion and obtain material. The material was deposited directly onto a glass slide. For each technique, one H&E-stained smear, one PAP-stained smear, and one MGG-stained smear were prepared. Smears for H&E and PAP were fixed with isopropyl alcohol; smears for MGG were air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized using the oral Bethesda system into NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC. For detection of malignancy, true-positive cases appear to include any cytological diagnosis other than NILM (i.e., LSIL, HSIL, or SCC considered positive/abnormal), with malignant histopathological diagnoses as the reference.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any abnormal cytology category (LSIL, HSIL, or SCC) on oral Bethesda system
comments_index_test: This is a 4-arm study (BR, BRCC, SR, SRCC) where all 27 patients received all four index tests simultaneously, meaning all arms share the same patient population. This violates independence assumptions for meta-analysis if multiple arms are included. Diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) was calculated only against histopathological results available in 23/27 cases (85.19%); 4 patients lacked histopathological follow-up. The low specificity (50%) is attributed by the authors to small sample size (only 2 true-negative/non-malignant cases). The study does not clearly report a pre-specified positivity threshold — it can be inferred from the statistical values table that any non-NILM result = positive for malignancy detection.

index_test_reagent_name: Brush cytology with cytocentrifugation using 15 mL normal saline (1250 rpm, 3 min)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions; patients were referred after clinical evaluation in the Department of Otorhinolaryngology. The most common site was buccal mucosa (74.07%), followed by tongue, hard palate, and lower alveolar region.
specimen_collection: A commercially available toothbrush (medium bristles) was used to obtain material from the lesion. The material obtained from the brush was then immersed in 15 mL normal saline solution for cytocentrifugation (BRCC technique).
technique: Material was obtained from the lesion using a commercially available toothbrush (medium bristles). The material from the brush was immersed in 15 mL normal saline, mixed well, and subjected to cytocentrifugation (Program No. 1: 1250 rpm for 3 min). For each technique, one H&E-stained smear, one PAP-stained smear, and one MGG-stained smear were prepared. Smears for H&E and PAP were fixed in isopropyl alcohol; MGG smears were air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized per oral Bethesda system into NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC. For malignancy detection, statistical values calculated using Galen and Gambino method; BR and BRCC techniques showed 21 true-positive cases, 1 false-positive case, 0 false-negative cases, 1 true-negative case, sensitivity 100%, specificity 50%.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LSIL, HSIL, or SCC (any abnormal Bethesda category) for malignancy detection
comments_index_test: All four arms (BR, BRCC, SR, SRCC) were applied to the same 27 patients at the same visit; the BRCC specimen is derived directly from the same brush used for the BR arm (brush material immersed in saline after direct smear preparation). Arms are therefore not independent — the BRCC and BR arms share the same source material from each patient. This interdependence should be considered if any arm-level accuracy estimates are used in meta-analysis. Additionally, histopathology was only available for 23/27 cases, so diagnostic accuracy calculations are based on n=23.

index_test_reagent_name: Modified scrape cytology using commercially available plastic ice cream spoon; smear deposited directly onto glass slide
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions; most common sites were buccal mucosa, tongue, hard palate, and lower alveolar region. No specific systematic site-selection protocol beyond targeting the visible clinically suspected lesion is described.
specimen_collection: Material scraped from the lesion using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon and deposited directly onto a glass slide.
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline before the procedure. A commercially available plastic ice cream spoon was used to scrape material from the lesion. The material was deposited onto a glass slide. For each technique, one H&E-stained smear, one PAP-stained smear, and one MGG-stained smear were prepared; smears for H&E and PAP were fixed with isopropyl alcohol, and smears for MGG were air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized according to the oral Bethesda system into four diagnostic categories: negative for intraepithelial lesion (NILM), low-grade squamous intraepithelial neoplasia (LSIL), high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). For malignancy detection, any category other than NILM constitutes a positive result (inferred from sensitivity/specificity calculations).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any category other than NILM (LSIL, HSIL, or SCC)
comments_index_test: The SR arm had 2 non-diagnostic cases (7.41%) where a definitive cytological diagnosis could not be offered, reducing the analyzable denominator from 27 to 25. For the histopathological concordance analysis, SR offered diagnosis in 21/23 cases (one adenoid cystic carcinoma case was unsatisfactory due to only hemorrhagic material). All four index tests (BR, BRCC, SR, SRCC) were performed on the same 27 patients — arms are not independent; all patients received all four tests. This paired design should be accounted for in meta-analysis. The positivity threshold for binary malignancy classification is not explicitly pre-specified; it is inferred from the sensitivity/specificity results as NILM = negative vs. LSIL/HSIL/SCC = positive.

index_test_reagent_name: Scrape cytology with cytocentrifugation using 15 mL normal saline (1250 rpm, 3 min)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions in patients referred to the Department of Pathology. The most common site was the buccal mucosa, followed by tongue, hard palate, and lower alveolar region. Cases where the site was inaccessible for sampling were excluded.
specimen_collection: Scraping of the oral lesion using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon. The scraped material was then immersed in 15 mL normal saline for subsequent cytocentrifugation.
technique: Material was obtained by scraping the oral lesion with a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon (SR technique). The scraped material was then immersed in 15 mL normal saline, mixed well, and subjected to cytocentrifugation using program No. 1 (1250 rpm for 3 min). From the cytocentrifuged deposit, three smears were prepared: one stained with H&E (fixed in isopropyl alcohol), one with PAP (fixed in isopropyl alcohol), and one with MGG (air-dried).
positivity_threshold: Lesions were categorized according to the oral Bethesda system into four diagnostic categories: negative for intraepithelial lesion (NILM), low-grade squamous intraepithelial neoplasia (LSIL), high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). For diagnostic accuracy of malignancy detection, malignant cytological diagnoses (SCC/HSIL) were compared against histopathological diagnosis.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: SCC or dysplastic category (LSIL/HSIL/SCC) by oral Bethesda system; malignancy positive = SCC
comments_index_test: All four index test arms (BR, BRCC, SR, SRCC) were applied to the same 27 patients in a paired/within-subject design, meaning test results across arms are not independent. For SRCC, 27 patients received the test but definitive diagnosis was offered in only 26 (Table 1 n=26). Diagnostic accuracy against histopathology (available in 23/27 cases) was calculated on 22 cases for SRCC (Table 3: diagnosis offered in 22/23). Low sample size (n=27) limits reliability of sensitivity/specificity estimates. Specificity was only 50% across all arms, likely due to low sample size and high malignancy prevalence. The study uses 'complete concordance' and 'partial concordance' criteria rather than standard TP/FP/TN/FN from a pre-specified positivity threshold, which may affect comparability with other studies.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious lesions identified during systematic oral examination. The mucosa of the intended (suspicious) area was dried and the dye applied to that specific site.
technique: Solution A: 1% malachite, dimethyl-sulfoxide, glycerol and 1% methylene blue. Solution B: purified water, raspberry flavor, 1% lactic acid (pre- and post-rinse). Protocol: (1) Participants rinsed with Solution B for 20 seconds. (2) Mucosa of the intended area was dried with a triple syringe and gauze. (3) Solution A was applied. (4) After a 20-second wait, patients rinsed again with Solution B for 20 seconds. (5) Stain intensity was assessed by one observer after the final rinse. Cotton rolls were used to apply Solution B to clear the stained surface if needed; retained stain = positive.
positivity_threshold: The indicators of positive reaction include local, stipules and concentrated blue stains while wide and faint blue stains indicate a negative reaction. If the stain retained [after rinsing with Solution B], positive result was recorded and vice versa.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: localized, concentrated (deep) blue stain retention after rinse
comments_index_test: Single-arm study (methylene blue only, compared to biopsy as reference standard). One observer assessed staining intensity; no inter-rater reliability or calibration reported, introducing potential bias. No precancerous lesions were found in the sample (all histopathology results were either malignant or benign), limiting generalizability to premalignant detection. High malignancy prevalence (83.1%) may inflate sensitivity estimates. The biopsy was targeted to the area of highest dye uptake, which means the reference standard and index test were not fully independent — this could affect specificity and PPV estimates.

site_selection_index_test: The entire oral cavity was examined systematically; every suspect region was marked according to the Roed-Petersen topographical classification of the oral mucosa.
technique: All patients were seen and examined by the same experienced maxillofacial surgeon. A routine clinical examination was performed according to the standard protocol (reference 14), and the Roed-Petersen protocol was completed. The oral cavity was inspected under incandescent (white) light. Every suspect region was marked according to the Roed-Petersen classification. If a suspect lesion was identified during clinical examination, the surgeon took all clinical aspects into account (e.g., inflammation) to determine whether additional biopsy was necessary.
positivity_threshold: CA was positive when a suspect lesion was seen (negative CA = 0, positive CA = 1).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: suspect lesion visible on white-light examination
comments_index_test: This is a within-patient comparison study: all 195 patients received both the conventional white-light examination (CA) and VELscope autofluorescence examination sequentially by the same surgeon. The arms are therefore not independent. The surgeon was aware of both test results before the biopsy decision, introducing potential review bias. CA-alone accuracy is reported as 88.9% in text; sensitivity/specificity for CA alone are not formally reported separately from the combined CA+AF analysis. The reported sensitivity 95.2% and specificity 100% refer to the combined CA+AF approach. Meta-analysts should note that CA-alone diagnostic performance can only be partially inferred from the logistic regression tables.

index_test_commercial_name: VELscope (Visual Enhanced Lesion scope; Mectron, Cologne, Germany)
site_selection_index_test: The entire oral cavity was examined using VELscope in all patients during follow-up. Every suspect region was marked according to the Roed-Petersen classification.
technique: Examinations took place in a separate room with dimmed lights. Safety goggles were worn by both patients and the examiner throughout the inspection. The oral cavity was examined using VELscope (Mectron, Cologne, Germany) and a Pentax reflex camera. Every suspect region was marked according to the Roed-Petersen protocol. A suspect finding was defined as loss of fluorescence. Additional diascopy was performed to detect inflammation; patients with inflammatory lesions were re-examined after 14 days.
positivity_threshold: A suspect finding in the VELscope assessment was defined as loss of fluorescence (negative AF = 0; positive AF = 1).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (fluorescence loss)
comments_index_test: The same surgeon performed both the conventional clinical examination (CA) and the VELscope (AF) examination in all patients, raising concerns about lack of independence between the two test results and potential incorporation bias. Biopsy (reference standard) was only performed in 39/195 patients deemed suspect by either test; the remaining 156 patients were assumed to be recurrence-free without histological verification, which likely artificially inflates specificity (recorded as 100%). This partial verification is a major limitation for meta-analytic use of sensitivity/specificity figures.

site_selection_index_test: The cytobrush was applied to the clinically identified oral lesion (malignant or potentially malignant) in each patient — targeted application to the visible lesion site.
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient before biopsy using a cytobrush applied all over the lesion, and stored in PreservCyt ThinPrep (Hologic) liquid-based medium.
technique: Cytobrush smear collected from the lesion and stored in PreservCyt ThinPrep.
