Three cytologic slides were prepared for each lesion sample using the Cellspin I semi-automated cytocentrifuge (TharmacGmbH). Slides were stained according to the Papanicolaou method and classified using an adaptation of Remmerbach et al., with results categorized as: insufficient; negative for intraepithelial lesion and malignancy; low-grade lesion (ASC-US, LSIL); high-grade lesion (ASC-H, HSIL); suspicious for malignancy; or SCC. Two cytologists performed analyses, compared results, and discrepancies were discussed with a third cytologist.
positivity_threshold: High-risk cytologic result (high-grade lesion, suspicious for malignancy, or SCC) = positive; low-risk result (negative for intraepithelial lesion and malignancy, or low-grade lesion) = negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: high-grade lesion, suspicious for malignancy, or SCC on Papanicolaou cytology
calibration_of_assessors: No formal pre-study calibration or training exercise is described. Discrepancies between two cytologists were resolved by discussion with a third cytologist during the study.
comments_index_test: The study presents results for brush cytology both alone and combined with DNA-ICM (a second index-test arm). Results are also reported in a subgroup restricted to high-risk sites (floor of mouth, tongue; n=34 subset from Table VI). The 88 analyzed patients for cytology exclude 10 with inadequate cytology samples (from 98 total enrolled). The paper uses an adapted Remmerbach et al. classification, not the standard Bethesda system, though categories are analogous. The DNA-ICM arm was performed on the same slides after Papanicolaou staining (Feulgen re-stain), creating dependency between the two arms; meta-analysts should avoid double-counting patients.

index_test_commercial_name: MotiCyte DNA Cytology Work Station (Motic); Motic BA410 microscope; Moticam Pro 285A
site_selection_index_test: DNA-ICM was applied to the same slide prepared from the oral lesion smear collected by cytobrush 'all over the lesion'. High-risk site subgroup (floor of mouth, tongue) was also analyzed separately.
specimen_collection: Cytobrush smear collected from each patient's oral lesion (all over the lesion) before biopsy, stored in PreservCyt ThinPrep (Hologic). Three cytologic slides were prepared using Cellspin I semi-automated cytocentrifuge system (TharmacGmbH). The DNA-ICM was performed on the same slide as cytology after uncovering from Papanicolaou stain.
technique: Slides were uncovered in xylene and stained by the Feulgen-Schiff method (Merck) per manufacturer's instructions. DNA ploidy analyses were performed using the MotiCyte DNA Cytology Work Station (Motic) with a Motic BA410 microscope and Moticam Pro 285A color video camera. Nuclear content analysis followed the 4th ESACP Consensus in DNA image cytometry. For calibration, at least 35 nuclei of normal oral epithelial cells were selected; integrated optical density values were converted to reference values of 2c; coefficient of variation of reference cells <5% required. After calibration, a minimum of 200 nuclei per slide were randomly selected (cells with suspicious nuclear morphology were additionally included). Results classified as euploid or aneuploid using MotiCyte software version 2.
positivity_threshold: The sample was considered aneuploid if a stemline DNA index was <0.90 and >1.10 or <1.80 and >2.20 or <3.60 and >4.40 or if there were cells with exceeding 9c content. The sample was considered euploid if it did not fit these criteria.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: DNA aneuploidy (stemline DI outside 0.90–1.10, 1.80–2.20, 3.60–4.40, or any cell >9c)
calibration_of_assessors: No explicit assessor training or calibration prior to study described. Instrument calibration was performed per slide using at least 35 normal oral epithelial cell nuclei with coefficient of variation <5% required.
comments_index_test: DNA-ICM was performed on the same slide previously stained by Papanicolaou for cytology, meaning the DNA-ICM analyst likely had access to the cytologic findings on the same slide — potential for co-interpretation bias. The combined arm (brush cytology + DNA-ICM) was declared positive only if both methods were positive, which is a conjunctive rule; this increases specificity but may reduce sensitivity. 16 samples were inadequate (cytology and/or DNA-ICM), with 15 inadequate specifically for DNA-ICM; these were excluded from analysis, which could introduce verification or exclusion bias. The study reports results both for the full cohort (n=83 for DNA-ICM) and for a high-risk site subgroup (floor of mouth/tongue), which inflates apparent performance in the subgroup.

index_test_reagent_name: Papanicolaou stain combined with Feulgen-Schiff stain
index_test_commercial_name: PreservCyt ThinPrep (Hologic); MotiCyte DNA Cytology Work Station (Motic)
site_selection_index_test: The cytobrush smear was taken from each patient's identified oral lesion (clinically malignant or potentially malignant oral cavity lesion). The smear was taken 'all over the lesion.' High-risk anatomical sites (floor of mouth, tongue) were analyzed as a sub-group.
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient before biopsy using a cytobrush applied all over the lesion and stored in PreservCyt ThinPrep (Hologic). Three cytologic slides were prepared from each sample using a Cellspin I semi-automated cytocentrifuge system (TharmacGmbH). The same slides were used for both Papanicolaou staining (cytology) and subsequently for Feulgen-Schiff staining (DNA-ICM).
technique: Cytology: Slides stained by Papanicolaou and classified using an adaptation of Remmerbach et al. into: insufficient; negative for intraepithelial lesion/malignancy; low-grade lesion (ASC-US, LSIL); high-grade lesion (ASC-H, HSIL); suspicious for malignancy; or SCC. Two cytologists analysed slides, compared results, and discussed discrepancies with a third cytologist. DNA-ICM: Slides were uncovered in xylene and stained by Feulgen-Schiff method (Merck) per manufacturer instructions. Analysis performed using MotiCyte DNA Cytology Work Station (Motic) with Motic BA410 microscope and Moticam Pro 285A camera. At least 35 normal oral epithelial cell nuclei selected for calibration (CV <5%). After calibration, minimum 200 nuclei randomly selected per slide; cells with suspicious nuclear morphology also arbitrarily included. Data analysed with MotiCyte software v2. Combined result: classified as positive only when both cytology (high-risk) and DNA-ICM (aneuploid) were positive.
positivity_threshold: Combined result classified as positive when both brush cytology AND DNA-ICM were positive. Cytology positive (high-risk) = high-grade lesion, suspicious for malignancy, or SCC. DNA-ICM positive (aneuploid) = stemline DNA index <0.90 and >1.10, or <1.80 and >2.20, or <3.60 and >4.40, or cells with exceeding 9c content.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: both cytology high-risk AND DNA aneuploid
calibration_of_assessors: For DNA-ICM: instrument calibration used at least 35 normal oral epithelial cell nuclei as reference, with a coefficient of variation <5% adopted as quality assurance. For cytology: two cytologists performed analyses, compared results, and discussed discrepancies with a third cytologist (no formal pre-study training/calibration exercise explicitly described).
comments_index_test: This arm combines brush cytology (Papanicolaou) and DNA-ICM on the same slide. The combined result is defined as positive only when BOTH methods are positive, which increases specificity at the cost of sensitivity compared to either method alone. The n_patients_analyzed (54) is substantially smaller than n_patients_received (98) because 16 samples were inadequate for cytology and/or DNA ploidy, and only patients with evaluable results from both methods contributed to the combined analysis. The 44 patients excluded from combined analysis represent a significant attrition. No explicit blinding of assessors to the reference standard or clinical information is reported. A sub-group analysis restricted to high-risk anatomical sites (tongue, floor of mouth) reports improved performance (sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 100%), but the n for this sub-group is not explicitly stated (approx. 34 patients based on Table VI percentages).

site_selection_index_test: VelScope applied to oral lesions already identified through COE in patients with OPMDs/suspected malignancies; COE encompassed manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites.
technique: The VelScope device was used maintaining a distance of approximately 5 cm from the oral cavity to optimize visualization of natural tissue fluorescence. If necessary, the operating theatre was darkened to reduce natural light to an acceptable level. Loss of autofluorescence (LAF) — darker areas compared to surrounding tissue — was noted.
positivity_threshold: In the presence of LAF [loss of autofluorescence], the Vel-E is defined positive; dysplastic tissue should show darker aspects in comparison with the surrounding areas due to the loss of fluorescence (LAF).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (darker area vs. surrounding tissue)
calibration_of_assessors: No calibration or training was undertaken by the unskilled general dentist (u-GD) for the VelScope examination. The u-GD serves as the untrained comparator in this study.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Both examiners performed VelScope examination in the absence of histological data (blinded to reference standard results when performing the index test).
blinding_index_test_examiner: The u-GD examiner was NOT blinded to clinical information; the VelScope examination was performed 'on the basis of clinical information', meaning the examiner had access to clinical findings from COE when interpreting VelScope results.
comments_index_test: Both the u-GD and s-GD arms examined the same 35 patients, so the two arms are not independent — this introduces correlation that should be accounted for in any meta-analysis. The VelScope examination was conducted sequentially after COE on the same visit, and COE results were known to the examiner when interpreting VelScope, which may inflate apparent performance by anchoring. The u-GD arm is defined by absence of training, making it essentially a 'naive user' arm.

site_selection_index_test: VelScope was applied to oral lesions identified during clinical oral examination (COE) in patients presenting with suspected oral mucosal lesions. Examination encompassed intra-oral sites where lesions were clinically detected.
technique: The VelScope device was held at approximately 5 cm from the oral cavity to optimize visualization of natural tissue fluorescence. The operating theatre was darkened if necessary to reduce natural light. Both examiners interpreted the examination based on presence or absence of loss of autofluorescence (LAF). The skilled general dentist (s-GD) had completed a 1-year oral medicine training programme prior to performing the examination.
positivity_threshold: In the presence of LAF (loss of autofluorescence), the Vel-E is defined positive; dysplastic tissue should show darker aspects in comparison with the surrounding areas due to the loss of fluorescence (LAF).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (LAF / darker area)
calibration_of_assessors: The skilled general dentist (s-GD) completed a 1-year post-graduate training program in oral medicine at the Oral Medicine Unit, Federico II University of Naples, Italy, prior to performing examinations in the study. This included clinical sessions focused on improving competence in detecting OPMDs/OSCC.
blinding_index_test_assessors: VelScope examinations were performed before histopathological results were available; the reference standard (histopathology) was obtained subsequent to VelScope examination. However, the paper does not explicitly state that VelScope assessors were formally blinded to histopathology results.
blinding_index_test_examiner: The examiners performed VelScope after COE and after obtaining clinical history; they were not blinded to clinical information. The paper states examinations were performed 'on the basis of clinical information'. No formal blinding to patient demographics or history is reported.
comments_index_test: 1. The same 35 patients were examined by both u-GD and s-GD, making the two arms correlated/non-independent — this must be accounted for in any meta-analysis. 2. The margins of the biopsy incision were guided by the VelScope result ('The margins of the incision are guided by the result of the Vel-E'), introducing potential incorporation bias. 3. The study is described as a pilot with a small sample size (n=35), limiting precision of estimates. 4. The s-GD and u-GD arms cannot be treated as independent study populations for meta-analytic pooling.

index_test_reagent_name: Feulgen-thionin staining with DNA image cytometry
index_test_commercial_name: GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System DNA Image Cytometer (DNA-ICM)
site_selection_index_test: The brush was applied to the clinically characterized oral mucosal lesions (the site of the presenting lesion). Incisional biopsies were performed at the same locations where brush samples were obtained.
specimen_collection: The patient was instructed to rinse the mouth with water; the clinician then gently scraped the oral mucosal lesion at least 10 times using a flexible cotton cytology brush. The brush head was stored in a tube with cell preservation solution and sent to the laboratory within 24 hours.
technique: Brush samples were processed as liquid-based thin-layer cell preparations and stained with the Feulgen-thionin technique (stains nuclei dark blue without staining cytoplasm). Slides were scanned with the GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System DNA Image Cytometer (DNA-ICM). DNA quantitative analysis was performed only when specimens contained at least 300 epithelial cell nuclei normalized to normal epithelial cell nuclei. The DNA index (DI) — ratio of analysed sample nuclei DNA content to reference normal nuclear DNA content — was used to classify nuclei: diploid (DI 0.75–1.25), hyperdiploid (1.25–1.75), tetraploid (1.25–2.3), and aneuploid (DI ≥2.3).
positivity_threshold: If the aneuploid group has more than 3 nuclei (1% of at least 300 nuclei), or the hyperdiploid group had 5% of the total number of nuclei, or the tetraploid group had 10% of the total number of nuclei, the oral specimen was classified as having abnormal DNA content.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: abnormal DNA content (aneuploid >3 nuclei [DI≥2.3], or hyperdiploid ≥5%, or tetraploid ≥10%)
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA image cytometry was performed blinded to the histological results.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper does not report whether the DNA-ICM assessors were blinded to patient clinical information (age, diagnosis, habits). Blinding is only stated with respect to histological results.
comments_index_test: The study includes three disease subgroups (OSF, OLK, OSF+OLK) analyzed separately and combined; sensitivity/specificity are reported per subgroup and per dysplasia severity grade, enabling subgroup-level extraction. Cotton cytology brushes used (authors note this as a limitation potentially reducing accuracy vs. extended-tip brushes). The study is cross-sectional. Authors note DNA-ICM results may precede histological changes, which may explain some false-positive results. Minimum cellularity threshold of 300 nuclei required for analysis — cases not meeting this threshold are not mentioned as exclusions but could affect analyzable sample count.

index_test_reagent_name: DNA image cytometry using liquid-based brush biopsy; cut-off: DI ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c)
site_selection_index_test: The cytobrush was applied at the same location as the clinically identified OPMD lesion — i.e., targeted application to the lesion site rather than systematic whole-mouth examination.
specimen_collection: Brushing of the whole lesion surface using a liquid-based brush kit (MotiSavant, Motic, Xiamen, China).
technique: Each patient underwent cytobrush biopsy at the same lesion location before scalpel biopsy. The brush sample was collected by brushing the whole lesion with a liquid-based brush kit (MotiSavant, Motic, Xiamen, China). DNA content was then analyzed using ICM as previously described and per the manufacturer's protocol (MotiSavant). The optimal cut-off of at least 1 aneuploid cell with a DI ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c) was determined using the maximum Youden index from ROC curve analysis.
positivity_threshold: At least 1 aneuploid cell with a DI ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c); optimal cut-off determined by maximum Youden index.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: ≥1 aneuploid cell with DNA index ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c)
calibration_of_assessors: NR — no explicit training or calibration protocol for DNA-ICM assessors is described. The analyses were conducted by two named individuals (C.L. and Y.Z.) with reference to previous published methods and the manufacturer's protocol.
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM assessors were blinded to histopathological results; DNA content analyses were completed before histopathological diagnoses were made.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper does not explicitly state whether the DNA-ICM assessors were blinded to clinical information (patient history, demographics, lesion site, lesion type) when performing the DNA content analysis.
comments_index_test: The study has two arms: DNA-ICM alone (DI ≥ 3.5) and a combined risk model (DNA-ICM + lesion site + lesion type, risk score ≥ 4). This row covers only the DNA-ICM alone arm. The positivity threshold (DI ≥ 3.5) was determined empirically within the training set using maximum Youden index, which introduces optimism bias; it was then applied to the test set. The n_patients_analyzed of 765 (vs. 810 enrolled) reflects 45 patients with missing data noted in Figure 1A; this discrepancy should be flagged for risk-of-bias assessment (partial verification or missing index test results). The study unit is patients, not lesions.

index_test_reagent_name: Risk model combining DNA-ICM (DI ≥ 3.5) + lateral/ventral tongue site + non-homogenous lesion type; risk score cut-off ≥ 4
site_selection_index_test: The cytobrush was applied at the same location as the OPMD lesion (whole lesion brushed); clinical features (lesion site: lateral/ventral tongue vs. others; lesion type: homogenous vs. non-homogenous) were assessed for each patient's presenting OPMD lesion.
specimen_collection: Brush biopsy of the whole OPMD lesion using a liquid-based brush kit (MotiSavant, Motic, Xiamen, China). Cytobrush was performed before scalpel biopsy at the same lesion location.
technique: The risk model integrates three variables scored by β-coefficients from multivariate logistic regression: (1) DNA-ICM of brush biopsy specimen — at least 1 aneuploid cell with DI ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c) scores 2.57; (2) lesion site = lateral/ventral tongue scores 1.97; (3) lesion type = non-homogenous scores 2.03. The total risk score for each patient (range 0–6.57) is the sum of the applicable variable scores. A risk score ≥ 4 is classified as positive for carcinoma within OPMD. DNA-ICM analysis was performed using MotiSavant (Motic) per manufacturer's protocol.
positivity_threshold: Risk score ≥ 4 (sum of β-coefficient-based scores: lateral/ventral tongue = 1.97, non-homogenous type = 2.03, DI ≥ 3.5 = 2.57; total score range 0–6.57)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: composite risk score ≥ 4 (DNA-ICM DI ≥ 3.5 + lateral/ventral tongue + non-homogenous type)
calibration_of_assessors: DNA-ICM analyses were conducted by two named individuals (C.L. and Y.Z.); no formal calibration or training exercise is described for the clinical feature assessors. The histopathological diagnoses were performed by 2 oral pathologists.
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM assessors were blinded to histopathological results. The clinical feature components of the risk model (lesion site, lesion type) were assessed clinically; blinding of clinical assessors to the reference standard is not explicitly stated.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper does not describe whether those assessing clinical features (lesion site, lesion type) for the risk model were blinded to patient history or prior diagnoses. DNA-ICM analysts were blinded to histopathology but no statement about blinding to clinical information is provided.
comments_index_test: The Risk Model arm is a composite combining a laboratory test (DNA-ICM) with two clinical features (lesion site: lateral/ventral tongue; lesion morphology: non-homogenous). Performance was assessed separately in training (n=608, AUC 0.93) and test (n=202, AUC 0.94) sets. Note that 45 patients appear to have missing data per the flowchart annotation ('total: 765, 45 missing'), so the effective analyzed numbers may be 765 rather than 810 — the paper does not explicitly clarify this discrepancy. This arm overlaps fully with the DNA-ICM-only arm (same patients/specimens), which should be considered when assessing independence in meta-analysis.

index_test_reagent_name: 1% Rose Bengal dye (1 gm RB powder in 100 mL distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to the most representative mucosal site for white and red lesions, as identified by thorough intraoral clinical examination (CP1)
technique: Patients rinsed mouth with distilled water for 1 minute, followed by application of 1% RB solution (1 g RB powder in 100 mL distilled water) for 2 minutes over the clinically assessed site. Patients then rinsed mouth with distilled water for 1 minute to remove excess dye. Intraoral examination of the stained lesional area was carried out and staining intensity was evaluated visually as mild, moderate, intense, or negative.
positivity_threshold: Staining intensity evaluated visually as mild, moderate, intense (positive) or negative; hyperchromatic areas owing to increased stain intake (due to increased nuclear cytoplasmic ratio) considered indicative of dysplasia. Any degree of staining (mild, moderate, or intense) appears to constitute a positive result based on sensitivity/specificity calculations.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any stain uptake (mild, moderate, or intense); negative: no staining
blinding_index_test_assessors: NR for RB staining assessor. A blinding statement is made for the microbiopsy observer ('The observer was blinded to the result of vital staining and scalpel biopsy') but no explicit blinding of the RB staining assessor to reference standard results is stated.
comments_index_test: All three procedures (RB staining, microbiopsy, scalpel biopsy) were performed concomitantly on the same lesion in the same session, minimizing positional or time-lapse bias but also meaning that the RB staining result was visible to the clinician before microbiopsy and scalpel biopsy were performed. The binary positivity threshold used for sensitivity/specificity calculations is not explicitly stated — any degree of staining (mild/moderate/intense) appears to be considered positive by inference from Table/Fig-6. Small sample size (n=26, all male) and pilot design limit generalizability. Staining intensity categories (mild, moderate, intense) are not further defined with colorimetric or objective criteria.

site_selection_index_test: Microbiopsy was performed at the same site as the RB staining — the most representative mucosal site for the white/red lesion identified by thorough intraoral clinical examination, specifically targeting the intensely stained region.
specimen_collection: Tissue fragments were collected by scraping the lesional area gently with the sharp edge of a 3 mm dermatological ring curette until pinpoint mucosal bleeding was obtained (to ensure the basal layer had been sampled). Multiple tissue fragments were then routinely processed, embedded, and sectioned for H&E staining.
technique: A 3 mm diameter dermatological ring curette was applied to the intensely RB-stained region. The lesional area was scraped gently by the sharp edge of the curette until pinpoint mucosal bleeding was obtained (to confirm basal layer sampling). Multiple tissue fragments were routinely processed, embedded, and sectioned for H&E staining. Sections were coded randomly and observed under a light microscope. Epithelial dysplasia was graded using Banoczy J and Csiba A criteria. Most procedures were performed under infiltrative local anaesthesia.
positivity_threshold: Histopathological indicators of epithelial dysplasia (cellular and architectural changes) observed after microbiopsy, graded using criteria given by Banoczy J and Csiba A (hyperkeratosis, mild dysplasia, moderate dysplasia, severe dysplasia). Any dysplastic change or hyperkeratosis was considered indicative of a positive result.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: histological evidence of dysplasia (any grade) or hyperkeratosis by H&E
calibration_of_assessors: Sections were coded randomly before microscopic observation, but no formal pre-study calibration or training of assessors is described.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The observer was blinded to the result of vital staining and scalpel biopsy when evaluating the microbiopsy sections (sections were coded randomly).
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper does not explicitly state whether the microbiopsy assessor was blinded to patient clinical history, demographics, or prior diagnoses.
comments_index_test: All three procedures (RB staining, microbiopsy, scalpel biopsy) were performed concomitantly on the same lesion in each patient, so microbiopsy site was guided by the RB staining result (intensely stained region). This means the microbiopsy and scalpel biopsy were not independently sited — both targeted the RB-positive area, which may introduce spectrum bias. The study is a small pilot (n=26, all male); 4/26 microbiopsy specimens were reported as 'tissue insufficient'. Reference standard (scalpel biopsy) was also performed at the same RB-stained site, which limits independence of reference standard from index test.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
index_test_reagent_name: Autofluorescence with dental curing lamp (440–480 nm, 1500 mW/cm2)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically identified lesions compatible with OPMDs or OSCC. The scanning was performed on the specific lesion after visual examination and photographic documentation of each lesion.
technique: Tissue was irradiated with an SDi Radii Xpert polymerizing lamp (SDI, Australia) at a wavelength of 440–480 nm and intensity of 1500 mW/cm² applied at a distance of 20 cm from the lesion. The irradiated tissue was observed through the GOCCLES® device and photographs were taken using the mobile camera filter included in the device kit with a Xiaomi Redmi Note 9S smartphone.
positivity_threshold: Lesions showing fluorescence loss, visible as brown or dark green areas through the device, were classified as GOCCLES® positive. Lesions without visible dark areas, where all tissue appeared within the green spectrum, were classified as GOCCLES® negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss visible as brown or dark green areas
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not blinded. The paper explicitly states lack of examiner blinding as a limitation: all procedures including biopsy site selection were performed by the same professional.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information. The same professional performed all procedures (visual examination, GOCCLES® scanning, TB staining, and biopsy), meaning the examiner was aware of all clinical information when interpreting the index test.
comments_index_test: Single examiner performed all procedures (visual exam, GOCCLES®, TB staining, biopsy site selection), introducing incorporation bias and precluding blinding. The paper acknowledges this as a limitation. Additionally, GOCCLES® and TB were performed in the same session before biopsy, meaning results of one test were potentially visible to the examiner when interpreting the other — creating co-test awareness bias. The combined analysis (GOCCLES® + TB) was restricted to the 18/32 cases with concordant results, which is a non-standard analytic approach and may inflate or distort combined test performance estimates.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: TB staining was applied to the same oral lesions clinically identified as compatible with OPMDs or OSCC during visual examination. No separate site-selection procedure is described for TB beyond examination of the already-identified lesion.
technique: TB staining was performed following the technique described by Mashberg (1983). Photographs were captured using a Canon EFS 60 mm camera with a Canon Macro Ring Lite MR-14EX ring flash. The guidelines described by Mashberg (1980) were followed to ensure accurate interpretation.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with intense blue staining were classified as positive for TB, while those with no staining or with only slight or diffuse staining were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: intense blue stain retention
calibration_of_assessors: No formal calibration procedure is described for TB assessors. The paper states that the guidelines described by Mashberg (1980) were followed to ensure accurate interpretation of staining results.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not blinded. The paper explicitly acknowledges the lack of examiner blinding, as all procedures were performed by the same professional.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded. All procedures — including GOCCLES® scanning, TB staining, and biopsy site selection — were performed by the same professional, who was not blinded to other clinical information.
comments_index_test: TB and GOCCLES® were performed by the same unblinded examiner on the same 32 patients, raising incorporation bias risk. The combined analysis was restricted to only 18 cases with concordant results, reducing the effective sample. TB technique referenced to Mashberg (1983) without full protocol replication in the paper. Inter-examiner variability in TB interpretation is acknowledged as a limitation in the discussion.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
index_test_reagent_name: GOCCLES® autofluorescence device combined with toluidine blue staining
index_test_commercial_name: GOCCLES® (Pierrel S.p.A, Italy) combined with toluidine blue
site_selection_index_test: Clinically identified lesions compatible with OPMDs or OSCC were examined. Each lesion was visually examined and its exact location documented (tongue, hard palate, buccal mucosa, keratinized gingiva, labial mucosa); both GOCCLES® and TB were then applied to the same identified lesion.
technique: GOCCLES®: tissue irradiated with SDi Radii Xpert polymerizing lamp (440–480 nm, 1500 mW/cm² at 20 cm distance); observed through GOCCLES® device; photographed with Xiaomi Redmi Note 9S with mobile camera filter. Toluidine blue: applied following Mashberg (1983) technique. Combined result evaluated only in 18 cases where both tests yielded concordant results (both positive or both negative).
positivity_threshold: Both GOCCLES® and TB yielded concordant positive results (GOCCLES® showing fluorescence loss as brown or dark green areas AND TB showing intense dark royal blue staining). Concordant negative = no fluorescence loss on GOCCLES® AND no/diffuse staining on TB.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: both GOCCLES® fluorescence loss and TB intense staining concordantly positive
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not blinded. The paper explicitly states as a limitation: 'the lack of examiner blinding, as all procedures including biopsy site selection were performed by the same professional.'
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information. All procedures (visual examination, GOCCLES® scanning, TB staining, and biopsy) were performed by the same professional, who had full access to clinical findings.
comments_index_test: The combined arm analysis is restricted to the 18/32 cases where GOCCLES® and TB yielded concordant results, introducing selection bias — discordant cases (n=14) are excluded from combined analysis, which may inflate or deflate accuracy estimates. This is not a formal combined rule (e.g., either-positive or both-positive) applied to all 32 patients, but rather a post-hoc subgroup of concordant cases. Meta-analysts should note that this combined arm does not represent an independent test applied to all patients and may not be comparable to combined test strategies in other studies.

site_selection_index_test: Samples were collected from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area identified by the oncosurgeon during physical examination.
specimen_collection: Cytology brush used to collect material from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area; harvested material transferred onto a glass slide taking care that minimum damage to cells was incurred.
technique: Material harvested by cytology brush was transferred to a glass slide; conventional alcohol-fixed smears were prepared and stained according to the Papanicolaou method; slides were interpreted by a cytopathologist using diagnostic categories: negative, atypical, suspicious, positive (malignant cells present), and not sufficient.
positivity_threshold: "positive" indicated malignant cells present; categories used: negative (normal squamous cells and reactive or inflammatory changes), atypical (atypical cells present), suspicious (dyskeratotic cells of the parabasal type or only a few malignant cells present), positive (malignant cells present), not sufficient (few or poorly preserved squamous cells).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: malignant cells present on PAP-stained smear (category 'positive'; unclear if 'suspicious' included)
comments_index_test: The paper does not explicitly state whether 'suspicious' category was combined with 'positive' to define a positive test result in the analysis; this ambiguity affects the stated sensitivity (76.67%, 23/30). The figure included in the paper (Figure 1) is labelled as 'fluorescence imaging of cells prepared from voided urine,' suggesting it may be a reused image from prior urology work rather than a new oral cancer image. All three index test arms were applied to the same 60 patients, so arms are not independent.

index_test_arm_label: Brush Cytology (VPAC Receptor Targeting with TP4303)
index_test_reagent_name: TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) with DAPI (4,6-Dimidino-2-phenylindole, Dihydrochloride)
site_selection_index_test: Samples collected from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area using a cytology brush
specimen_collection: Cytology brush used to collect material from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area; harvested material transferred onto a glass slide taking care that minimum damage to cells was incurred
technique: Glass slides with harvested brush cytology material were fixed in 97% alcohol. TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) was added to cover the entire cell area (~1 cm diameter), kept in dark at 22°C for ~20 minutes, then thoroughly rinsed with deionized water and air dried. 20 µl of DAPI (Fisher Scientific, PA) was added to the cells; a coverslip was placed and the slide observed under a fluorescent microscope. Positive cells (VPAC receptor-expressing malignant cells) showed dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus; negative cells (non-malignant) showed only blue DAPI-stained nucleus.
positivity_threshold: Positive for VPAC receptors (malignant cells): cells show dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus indicating TP4303 interaction with VPAC receptor molecules on the cell surface. Negative for VPAC receptors (non-malignant cells): only DAPI-bound cell nucleus seen in dark blue, indicating absence of VPAC receptors.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark orange fluorescence around nucleus (TP4303–VPAC receptor interaction)
comments_index_test: 1) Both the brush cytology VPAC arm and oral gargle VPAC arm were applied to the same 60 patients simultaneously, making the two arms non-independent — relevant for meta-analysis. 2) The figure labeled 'Fluorescence imaging of cells prepared from voided urine' appears to be recycled from prior bladder/prostate cancer work rather than being generated from oral specimens in this study — raises concern about validity of illustration. 3) No separate cytopathologist blinding is described; the same group applied and interpreted all tests. 4) This is described as a 'preliminary report', suggesting the findings should be interpreted with caution.

index_test_arm_label: Oral Gargle (VPAC Receptor Targeting with TP4303)
index_test_reagent_name: TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) with DAPI (4,6-Dimidino-2-phenylindole, Dihydrochloride); sample collected via normal saline gargle
site_selection_index_test: Whole oral cavity via gargle; patients gargled with normal saline to collect exfoliated cells shed in saliva from the entire oral cavity, rather than targeting a specific suspicious lesion site.
specimen_collection: Patients gargled with 20 cc of normal saline for a few minutes and spat the contents into a collecting cup. The collected fluid was centrifuged and the sediment was transferred onto a glass slide and fixed in 97% alcohol.
technique: Sediment from centrifuged oral gargle fixed in 97% alcohol on a glass slide. TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) added to cover the cell area (~1 cm diameter), kept in dark at 22°C for ~20 minutes, then thoroughly rinsed with deionized water and air dried. 20 µl DAPI (Fisher Scientific) added; coverslip placed and slide examined under fluorescent microscope. Cells with TP4303 interaction show dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus (VPAC receptor positive/malignant); absence of VPAC receptors shows only DAPI-bound nucleus in dark blue.
positivity_threshold: Cells with TP4303 interaction presenting with dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus indicate presence of VPAC receptor molecules around the cell surface = positive for VPAC receptors (malignant cells). In the absence of VPAC receptors, only the DAPI-bound cell nucleus is seen in dark blue = negative for VPAC receptors (non-malignant cells).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark orange fluorescence around nucleus (TP4303-VPAC receptor interaction)
comments_index_test: 1) The figure illustrating fluorescence microscopy technique (Figure 1) is captioned 'Fluorescence imaging of cells prepared from voided urine' — this appears to be a recycled figure from the same group's prior bladder/prostate cancer studies, not an oral cancer specimen, raising concerns about representativeness of the illustration. 2) No wash-out or carry-over concerns between arms as specimens are collected independently (gargle vs. brush). 3) The study uses patients as the unit of analysis; lesion-level data are not reported. 4) Conflict of interest declared: two authors hold patents on the TP4303 molecule, which may bias result reporting. 5) 'Accuracy' is reported (95%) but this figure differs slightly from what one would calculate from the 2x2 table provided (Table 3 shows 29 TP + 28 TN out of 60 = 95%), consistent with the text.

index_test_reagent_name: Blue light (400–460 nm excitation) with green fluorescence filter (520–560 nm / 470–580 nm)
site_selection_index_test: FV was applied to the presenting oral mucosal lesion identified during conventional oral examination. FV 'can be adapted to any area of the oral cavity.' The ROI of the lesion was defined as the area of FVL; a control ROI was set at a distance away in the same sub-site of the oral cavity in normal mucosa in front of the lesion without FVL and oral mucosal lesions.
technique: FV images were taken in a room that was as dark as possible. The irradiating light was set perpendicular to the lesion and the irradiation range was set to about 10 cm. ORALOOK® (excitation ~422 nm, filter 520–560 nm) and IllumiScan® (excitation 425 nm, filter 470–580 nm) were used randomly at the attending physician's discretion; both detect apple-green autofluorescence. FV images and oral conditions were compared visually (subjective evaluation) to evaluate FVR, FVA, or FVL. For objective evaluation, image processing analysis was performed on FV images using ImageJ v1.5; ROIs for the lesion (area of FVL) and a control area (same sub-site normal mucosa in front of lesion) were established, and G-value metrics (MeanV, MediV, SD, CV, skewness, kurtosis, VRatio) were extracted. Surface plots and colour mapping were produced for the lesion ROI. Positive/negative classification was determined by two or more screenings using the surface plot as a reference.
positivity_threshold: Subjective evaluation: 'we defined a positive case as FVL and a negative case as only FVA or FVR by two or more screenings using the surface plot as a reference.' Objective evaluation: cut-off values set by ROC analysis — e.g., MeanV < 52.5, MediV < 60.0, CV > 0.15, skewness > 0.71, VRatio < 87.5%.
positivity_threshold_transformed: Subjective: positive = fluorescence visualization loss (FVL); Objective: positive = G-value metrics exceeding ROC-derived cut-offs (e.g., VRatio < 87.5%, CV > 0.15)
comments_index_test: 1. Two different OI devices (ORALOOK® and IllumiScan®) were used interchangeably and randomly assigned by the attending physician; the authors assert these are equivalent but device-level subgroup analyses are not presented. 2. Both subjective and objective evaluations were derived from the same FV images in the same 502-patient cohort — these are not independent arms. 3. The study is retrospective, which limits generalisability. 4. No details on assessor training or blinding are provided, raising risk-of-bias concerns. 5. Conflicts of interest declared: study partly funded by Shofu Inc (IllumiScan® manufacturer) and HITS PLAN Inc (ORALOOK® manufacturer).

index_test_reagent_name: 425 nm blue light autofluorescence visualisation (green channel 490–550 nm)
site_selection_index_test: Lesions were identified during conventional oral examination under white light. A region of interest (ROI) was defined in the lesion area of the G-image based on intraoral photographs and intraoral findings by the attending physician. For NOM, ROIs were set at the sublingual mucosa, buccal mucosa, the transition area from the molar attachment gingiva to the buccal mucosa, and the mucosa on the floor of the oral cavity.
technique: Lesions were photographed using IllumiScan® in a dark room after white-light digital camera recording. The device emits 425 nm blue light; the distance between the lens and lesion was approximately 30 mm. Images were transferred to a computer and analysed using ImageJ v1.53. Each image was divided into RGB components and a black-and-white image (G-image) was created from the green component (490–550 nm). An ROI was defined in the lesion area. FI was expressed at 256 levels (0–255). Average FI, standard deviation (SD), and coefficient of variation (CV = [SD/average FI] × 10) were calculated for each ROI.
positivity_threshold: ROC-derived cut-off values: CV cut-off of 1.70 (sensitivity 72.9%, specificity 78.3%, AUC 0.84); average FI cut-off of 98.5 (sensitivity 71.2%, specificity 67.8%, AUC 0.72); SD cut-off of 11.2 (sensitivity 83.1%, specificity 65.6%, AUC 0.63). In multivariate analysis, only CV was independently significant (p = 0.038).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: CV ≥ 1.70 (higher coefficient of variation indicates SCC)
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded. The ROI was defined by the attending physician based on intraoral photographs and intraoral findings, indicating the examiner had full access to clinical information.
comments_index_test: This study uses quantitative image analysis (fluorescence intensity and CV) rather than visual binary classification (FVL vs. FVR). Positivity thresholds are derived post-hoc via ROC analysis, not pre-specified. The NOM control group was significantly younger (median age 36) than OML groups (median 70–75 years), which may confound FI comparisons. Unit of analysis is effectively one image/ROI per patient. The attending physician who defined ROIs was not blinded to clinical findings. The study compares SCC vs. non-SCC OMLs (lichen planus, epithelial dysplasia, carcinoma in situ) and NOM — not a typical binary diseased/non-diseased split, which complicates standard diagnostic accuracy calculations.

site_selection_index_test: The test was applied to clinically identified lesions suspicious for oral malignancy. The most common sites were the cheek and tongue, followed by the lip and floor of the mouth.
specimen_collection: The lesion was scraped using a coverslip to collect cells, which were then spread onto a glass slide and fixed in 80% alcohol. Two smears were collected per lesion using separate coverslips.
technique: Label two glass slides with patient name, date, and anatomic location. Remove excess saliva from the lesion area with gauze. Scrape the entire lesion vigorously with a coverslip (noticeable scraping, may cause minor bleeding, but not painful). Spread harvested cells onto the glass slide from the frosted end to the other end, ensuring white filmy debris is visible. Immediately place the slide in a Koplin jar containing 80% alcohol fixative to prevent cell degeneration. Repeat the same procedure for a second smear of the same lesion. Use a different coverslip for multiple lesions to prevent cell cross-contamination.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: Significant reporting inconsistencies: the text states 'total number of males was 53, and the females were 20' (n=73) but the age-sex table sums to 43 males and 23 females (n=66), and the stated male:female ratio of 1.9:1 matches neither figure (53/20=2.65; 43/23=1.87). The total number of patients who underwent exfoliative cytology is not explicitly stated. The NPV of 26.38% alongside sensitivity 83.4% and specificity 100% is mathematically consistent only with a very small number of true negatives, suggesting the enrolled population was almost entirely disease-positive — typical of a case series rather than a screening study. No positivity threshold for cytology interpretation is defined. No calibration or blinding procedures are reported, raising risk-of-bias concerns.

index_test_reagent_name: Papanicolaou (PAP) stain; fixative: 95% ethanol with 3% glacial acetic acid
site_selection_index_test: Not an in-vivo examination — the index test was applied to biopsy specimens (incisional, excisional, or punch biopsy) already collected from oral lesions provisionally diagnosed as OPMDs or oral malignant lesions. No separate site-selection procedure within the oral cavity was performed for this test.
specimen_collection: The specimen was the leftover formalin fixative fluid from the original specimen bottle in which the biopsy tissue was received. The fixative contains cells exfoliated from the biopsy cut surfaces. The obtained biopsy specimens were shifted to a container with fresh fixative, and the fixative fluid from the original bottle was then used for centrifugation.
technique: The fixative fluid from the original biopsy specimen bottle was centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes. The supernatant was discarded and the sediment was washed twice in normal saline. Smears were prepared on albumen-coated slides for good cell adherence. Smears were fixed in 95% ethanol with 3% glacial acetic acid (Biofix spray) and stained with Papanicolaou (PAP) stain. Smears were analysed by two observers.
positivity_threshold: Based on Shafer's classification: for OPMDs, cytological smears classified as Class II (atypia) or Class III (intermediate/severe dysplasia/CIS) were reported as positive; for oral malignant lesions, Class IV (suggestive of cancer) or Class V (positive for cancer) were reported as positive. Class I (normal) was reported as negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive (OPMDs): Class II–III (atypia/severe dysplasia); positive (malignant): Class IV–V (suggestive/positive for cancer)
calibration_of_assessors: Two observers analyzed the prepared smears to reduce inter-observer bias. No formal pre-study calibration or training exercise is described.
comments_index_test: This is not a conventional in-vivo oral diagnostic test but a laboratory-based cytology method performed on formalin fixative fluid from biopsy specimens. The unit of analysis is the lesion/biopsy specimen (n=30), not separate from the patient (each patient appears to have contributed one lesion). The positivity threshold differs by lesion category (OPMDs vs. malignant), which complicates single-threshold sensitivity/specificity reporting. The study reports overall diagnostic accuracy of 50% (80% for malignant lesions, 20% for OPMDs). Inconclusive results (n=4) were not classified as either positive or negative, which may affect accuracy calculations. Small sample size is a noted limitation.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious oral lesions identified on COE; all patients were recruited based on the presence of clinically suspicious oral lesions referred to the Department of Oral Pathology and Microbiology.
technique: After COE, autofluorescence visualization (AFV) was achieved using a handheld VELscope (C Ultra by Technomax Corporation, Pune, Maharashtra). Findings were categorized per manufacturer's literature as: AFL (Loss of fluorescence) or AFR (Retained or no loss of fluorescence). No further procedural steps (e.g., room lighting conditions, dwell time, distance) are described.
positivity_threshold: AFL: Loss of fluorescence (autofluorescence visualization loss) was classified as a positive result, indicating potential dysplasia or malignancy. 'When a lesion demonstrating FVL was confirmed to be malignant or dysplastic following histopathological assessment, it was designated as a true-positive (TP) result.'
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: autofluorescence loss (AFL)
blinding_index_test_assessors: The histopathologist (reference standard assessor) was blinded to VELscope findings, but the paper does not explicitly state whether the VELscope examiner was blinded to the reference standard (histopathology) results.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper states VELscope and COE were performed 'by different experts' but does not describe whether the VELscope examiner was blinded to patient clinical information, history, or demographics.
comments_index_test: The paper reports two separate 2×2 tables and diagnostic accuracy estimates: (1) all dysplasia+malignancy vs. no dysplasia (sensitivity 77.77%, specificity 25%, PPV 87.5%, NPV 16.67%); and (2) high-risk (moderate/severe dysplasia or carcinoma in situ) vs. low-risk (no/mild dysplasia) — sensitivity 90.47%, specificity 44.44%, PPV 79.16%, NPV 66.67%. Meta-analysts should select the appropriate threshold comparison. The study assumes one lesion per patient; lesion-level vs. patient-level analysis is not distinguished. No calibration or training of the VELscope examiner is reported. Small sample (n=30) from a single tertiary centre limits generalizability.

index_test_commercial_name: VELscope (LED Dental, Inc., White Rock, BC, Canada)
site_selection_index_test: The Velscope was applied to clinically diagnosed OPMD lesions in participants recruited from an oral health screening camp. All 40 participants with clinically diagnosed OPMDs underwent Velscope examination; no specific intra-oral site-selection protocol beyond examining the presenting OPMD lesion is described.
technique: Examinations were conducted in a dark room, with patients wearing special glasses provided in the Velscope kit. A blue light (400–460 nm) was directed onto the oral tissues, and the emitted fluorescence was assessed visually. Lesions exhibiting loss of autofluorescence (FVL) appeared as dark areas, suggesting dysplasia. Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate the visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study.
positivity_threshold: Lesions exhibiting loss of autofluorescence (FVL) appeared as dark areas, suggesting dysplasia.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (dark areas / fluorescence visualization loss)
calibration_of_assessors: Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate the visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study.
comments_index_test: 1. Apparent typographical error in Results: paper states 'Velscope identified 51 participants as positive' but total n=40 and contingency table shows 31 positive/9 negative — the figure 51 is likely a typo for 31. 2. Methods mention both 'incisional biopsy' and 'after final surgical resection' for tissue collection, creating ambiguity about the reference standard procedure. 3. The calibration of 10 patients is included within the study sample of 40, raising questions about whether calibration cases were included in the diagnostic accuracy analysis. 4. Single-arm study from a single screening camp with small sample size (n=40); results may not be generalizable. 5. Unit of analysis is patients with one lesion each (confirmed by Table 5 total = 40).

site_selection_index_test: Whole oral cavity examined; visual inspection surveying the whole oral cavity for any ulcerations, nodules, swelling, or alterations in color and textures, plus palpation of facial bones and soft tissues
technique: Conventional visual oral examination (VOE) performed by experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons (OMS). Technique comprises visual inspection of the whole oral cavity for ulcerations, nodules, swelling, or alterations in colour and texture, combined with palpation of facial bones and soft tissues to detect asymmetries, masses, and lymphadenopathy. Lesions were categorised as leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, possible oral cancer, ulcer, or other.
positivity_threshold: Abnormal VOE findings — leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possibly oral cancer — were identified as positive/abnormal findings. In the logistic regression models, VOE results were entered as a categorical covariate; 'possible oral cancer' was the category most strongly associated with OED/OSCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any abnormal VOE finding (leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, possible oral cancer)
calibration_of_assessors: NR — examiners were described as 'experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons (OMS)' and no significant difference in VOE judgment was reported across the three study sites, but no formal pre-study calibration or training exercise is described.
comments_index_test: This is a multi-arm study in which all 201 patients received both VOE and ZNF582m testing plus biopsy (reference standard). The primary analysis uses logistic regression with C-index/AUC rather than reporting a standard 2×2 contingency table; sensitivity and specificity for VOE alone are not directly reported in tabular form and would need to be derived from Table 1 data. The VOE is used as a categorical variable (multiple lesion types) in models rather than a binary positive/negative result, complicating direct extraction of diagnostic accuracy metrics for meta-analysis. Additionally, the study population comprised patients already self-referring with suspicious lesions at tertiary medical centres (not a community screening population), which may affect generalisability and prevalence estimates.

index_test_reagent_name: ZNF582 methylation (ZNF582m) via quantitative methylation-specific PCR (TaqMan-based)
index_test_commercial_name: Epigene ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit (iStat Biomedical Co., Ltd.)
site_selection_index_test: Specimen collected from the identified mucosal lesion in each patient after VOE examination; the oral exfoliated cell specimen was collected from the mucosal lesion site.
specimen_collection: Oral epithelial cells (OEC) collected using a foam brush and preserved in 'Epigene' Specimen Collection and Transfer Tube (iStat Biomedical Co., Ltd.).
technique: Genomic DNA (gDNA) extracted from OECs using the Epigene Nucleic Acid Extraction Kit. gDNA concentration quantified using NanoDrop 2000c Spectrophotometer. gDNA subjected to bisulfite conversion using Epigene Bisulfite Conversion Kit (converts unmethylated cytosine to uracil; methylated cytosine unchanged). Bisulfite-converted gDNA used for ZNF582m assay: ZNF582m levels determined using the Epigene ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit via quantitative methylation-specific PCR (TaqMan-based technology) with Light Cycler LC480. COL2A gene (containing non-CpG sequences) used as internal reference and validity indicator. Two Cp values determined (ZNF582 and COL2A); methylation qualitatively determined per manufacturer's instructions.
positivity_threshold: DNA methylation was qualitatively determined in accordance with manufacturer's instructions (no explicit numerical threshold stated in the paper).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: manufacturer-defined qualitative methylation positivity (Cp-based)
comments_index_test: 1. The study is funded by iStat Biomedical Co., Ltd. (manufacturer of the Epigene ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit), and three authors (Su Y-F, Juan Y-C, Fwu C-W) are employees of iStat Biomedical — significant conflict of interest. 2. The positivity threshold is not explicitly stated; it relies entirely on undisclosed manufacturer's instructions. 3. The primary analysis uses logistic regression/ROC C-index comparison rather than reporting a standard 2×2 contingency table at a single threshold, making direct sensitivity/specificity extraction at a pre-specified cut-off difficult. 4. All 201 patients received both index tests (ZNF582m and VOE) and the reference standard (biopsy), allowing paired analysis but also meaning arms are not independent. 5. The methylation test is performed on exfoliated cells from the lesion site (not a whole-mouth rinse), which should be noted for comparability with other ZNF582m studies using mouth rinse samples.

index_test_reagent_name: Blue excitation light 400-460 nm (excitation filter: 60-nm bandpass centered at 425 nm; emission filter: 475-nm long-pass)
site_selection_index_test: The whole oral cavity was examined with direct FV. After white-light assessment, room lights were turned off and the oral cavity was viewed with the direct FV device. Particular attention was paid to sites of previous lesions (i.e., sites of prior oral SCC). Lesion fluorescence was assessed in comparison to adjacent tissue and contralateral (anatomical control) tissue.
technique: Room lights were turned off and the oral cavity was illuminated with blue excitation light (400–460 nm; excitation filter: 60-nm bandpass centered at 425 nm) from the handheld unit. Tissue fluorescence was viewed directly through a coaxial viewing port in the handheld unit. An emission filter (475-nm long-pass) rejected blue excitation light, and a notch filter divided the fluorescent spectrum into red and green components. Normal mucosa appeared pale green; lesions with reduced fluorescence (dark green to black compared to adjacent and contralateral tissue) were classified as FV loss (FVL); lesions retaining normal green fluorescence were classified as FV retention (FVR).
positivity_threshold: Fluorescence loss (FVL): tissue showing a distinct reduction in the normal pale green autofluorescence, appearing as dark green to black, as assessed by comparison with adjacent tissue and contralateral (anatomical control) tissue.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (dark green to black vs. adjacent/contralateral normal tissue)
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not explicitly stated. The clinicians decided on biopsy based on standard clinical features and toluidine blue staining, not based on direct FV results ('The clinicians would then decide whether the oral lesions required biopsy based on standard clinical features... and not based on the direct FV examination'). However, blinding of FV assessors to histopathology results is not explicitly described.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR. The same clinicians who performed white-light assessment and toluidine blue evaluation also performed direct FV; no statement is made about blinding to clinical information during FV assessment.
comments_index_test: This is a pilot study with 44 patients (50 biopsy sites). Unit of analysis is lesions/biopsy sites. The study population was pre-selected (patients with known history of biopsy-confirmed oral dysplasia or SCC), introducing verification and spectrum bias — not a true screening population. The biopsy decision was made based on standard clinical criteria (not FV), which is a strength, but FV was performed by the same clinicians who did the clinical assessment, creating potential for unblinded interpretation. The histological distribution is skewed heavily toward invasive SCC (33/50), limiting generalizability. Photographs were acquired for documentation only and were not used for lesion classification — classification was based solely on direct visual impression.

index_test_reagent_name: Wooden Ayer's spatula; stained with Diff-Quik and Papanicolaou stains
site_selection_index_test: Scrape smears were taken from pathological sites, frequently from mucosal lesions and from other representative sites within the oral cavity (tongue, buccal mucosa, gingiva, palate, and other sites).
specimen_collection: Scrape smears collected using a wooden Ayer's spatula from pathological/mucosal lesion sites.
technique: Patients washed their oral cavity with water before sample collection. Scrape smears were collected using a wooden Ayer's spatula from pathological sites (mucosal lesions and other representative sites). Wet smears were fixed in 95% ethanol for Papanicolaou staining; air-dried smears were stained with Romanowsky (Diff-Quik) stain. Cytological findings were correlated with histopathological diagnosis.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: The paper reports both FNAC and scrape cytology as index tests applied to the same patients, but statistical performance metrics (sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic accuracy) appear to be reported for scrape cytology (or the combined cytology approach) rather than FNAC separately. It is unclear from the Methods whether FNAC and scrape cytology were always performed on all patients or selectively. The 128 enrolled / 118 analyzed counts likely apply to both arms combined. The accuracy figures (69.56% overall, 81.25% premalignant, 63.33% malignant) are attributed primarily to scrape cytology in the text. Meta-analysts should note the potential non-independence of FNAC and scrape cytology arms due to shared patients.

index_test_reagent_name: 23–24G needle, 10 ml disposable plastic syringe; stained with Diff-Quik and Papanicolaou stains
site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically localized oral lesions (growths, ulcerative lesions, whitish/reddish patches) identified during examination of the oral cavity. Sites included tongue, buccal mucosa, gingiva, palate, and other sites.
specimen_collection: Fine-needle aspiration using a 23–24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable plastic syringe; aspirated material spread on clean numbered slides.
technique: After localizing the lesion, a 23–24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable plastic syringe was used for aspiration. Aspirated material was spread on clean numbered slides. Wet smears were fixed in 95% ethanol for Papanicolaou stain; air-dried smears were stained with Romanowsky (Diff-Quik) stain. Cytological outcomes were correlated with histopathological diagnosis.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: FNAC and scrape cytology were both performed on all 118 analyzed patients, but the statistical results (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, diagnostic accuracy) presented in the paper appear to combine both methods under 'cytological diagnosis' without separating FNAC-specific performance from scrape cytology performance. The 69.56% overall diagnostic accuracy figure and the arm-specific figures (81.25% for premalignant, 63.33% for malignant) cannot be attributed exclusively to FNAC. This severely limits extraction of FNAC-specific diagnostic accuracy data for meta-analysis.

site_selection_index_test: Participants were screened for oral mucosal lesions, and those lesions were subjected to DrOroscope examination focusing on identifying dysplastic lesions. The device is described as intraoral, examining clinically diagnosed red, white, or mixed oral mucosal lesions.
technique: Participants with oral mucosal lesions were examined using the DrOroscope device. On blue light exposure (400–460 nm), normal tissues reflect green fluorescence, while abnormal (dysplastic) tissues show a loss of fluorescence and appear dark. Images were captured with the image sensor. Image analysis was performed using software algorithms generated from AI concepts. Based on the analysis, lesions were categorized as variable (no dysplastic changes), borderline (mild and moderate dysplastic changes), or severe/dysplasia (severe cases).
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized as 'borderline' (mild and moderate dysplastic changes) or 'dysplasia/severe' (severe cases) were considered positive; lesions categorized as 'variable' (no dysplastic changes) were considered negative. For binary analysis: variable = negative; borderline + dysplasia = positive.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (borderline or dysplasia category); negative: normal green fluorescence (variable category)
calibration_of_assessors: The examiner was trained in the operation of DrOroscope and interpreting its results. No further detail on the nature or extent of training is provided.
comments_index_test: Small sample size (n=40). The study appears to use one lesion per patient, making patient-level and lesion-level counts equivalent (both = 40). The binary positivity threshold (variable = negative; borderline + dysplasia = positive) is not explicitly stated but is inferred from Tables 3 and 4. The DrOroscope is a novel proprietary device developed by Raamah Biocare Pvt. Ltd. (acknowledged in the paper); no independent validation of the AI algorithm is described. The device examines lesions intraorally, unlike VELscope which is used extraorally — this is noted as a distinguishing feature. No detail on dwell time, distance from lesion, or standardized imaging protocol is provided.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically diagnosed suspicious lesions (oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, or oral submucous fibrosis) from a distance of approximately 3–4 inches. Targeted to the lesion area identified during initial clinical evaluation.
technique: A second investigator (separate from the clinician who made the initial diagnosis) performed the VELscope examination at approximately 3–4 inches distance from the tissue. The device emits blue-violet light (400–460 nm) to excite endogenous tissue fluorophores. The nature of tissue fluorescence was noted in terms of fluorescence retention (FVR) or fluorescence loss (FVL). Photographs of the fluorescence were recorded for documentation.
positivity_threshold: Fluorescence loss (FVL) — areas with dysplasia, inflammation, or increased vascularization lose fluorescence and appear dark — considered positive; normal oral mucosa retains pale green fluorescence (FVR) — considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (dark area)
calibration_of_assessors: NR — a separate investigator from the one who performed the initial clinical evaluation conducted the VELscope examination, but no specific training, calibration sessions, or inter-examiner reliability exercises are described.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not explicitly stated. The VELscope examination was performed before biopsy and histopathological analysis (sequential design), so the VELscope examiner could not have known the histopathology result at the time of assessment, but formal blinding is not declared.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Partial blinding attempted: the VELscope examination was performed by a different investigator than the one who conducted the initial clinical evaluation and provisional diagnosis, to minimize risk of bias. However, the paper does not explicitly state whether the VELscope examiner was blinded to the clinical diagnosis or patient history.
comments_index_test: 1) Very small sub-group sample sizes (n=10 per disease group) severely limit reliability of sensitivity/specificity estimates. 2) In OSMF, all 10 patients were VELscope-positive (100% sensitivity, 0% specificity), making diagnostic metrics uninterpretable — likely a floor effect or disease-specific artefact. 3) The study analyzes VELscope separately for each of the three OPMDs (OL, OLP, OSMF) rather than providing a pooled result, complicating cross-study comparison. 4) Blinding procedures are incompletely described; partial separation of examiners is noted but formal blinding protocols are absent. 5) The paper mislabels AUC interpretation: an AUC of 0.458 for VELscope in OL is described as 'closest to histopathology' but this is below chance level, suggesting a fundamental error in interpretation or ROC curve labeling.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the suspicious lesion area in patients clinically diagnosed with oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, or oral submucous fibrosis
technique: Toluidine blue was applied to the suspicious oral mucosal area. A dark blue (royal or navy) stain of either the entire lesion or a portion was considered positive; lack of colour absorption was considered negative; light or pale blue staining was considered doubtful. For doubtful cases, the lesion was wiped with a cotton swab dipped in 1% acetic acid — if staining disappeared, the result was negative; if it persisted, biopsy was indicated.
positivity_threshold: A dark blue (royal or navy) stain of either the entire lesion or a portion of it was considered positive; a lack of colour absorption by the lesion as negative; and light or pale blue staining as doubtful. Wiping with 1% acetic acid: if staining disappears = negative; if it persists = indicated for biopsy (positive).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue (royal or navy) stain retention after acetic acid wash
comments_index_test: This is a multi-arm study in which all 30 patients received all four index tests (VELscope, toluidine blue, methylene blue, Lugol's iodine), making the arms fully paired. Results are reported separately by OPMD subtype (OL, OLP, OSMF; n=10 each) rather than pooled across all 30, which limits overall diagnostic accuracy estimates. The unit of analysis appears to be one lesion per patient. Table 2 contains apparent data entry errors (raw counts rendered as decimals, e.g., '0.476(75%)'), which undermines confidence in the OLP data. Biopsy was performed irrespective of staining results, which supports unbiased reference standard ascertainment. The study does not report who performed the vital staining or whether this was the same investigator who conducted clinical evaluation, raising potential for performance bias.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the clinically identified suspicious area (the oral lesion diagnosed as OL, OLP, or OSMF)
technique: Methylene blue was applied to the suspicious oral lesion area. Deep blue stains that were local, stippled and patchy were considered positive; faint blue stains that were wide, shallow and easily washable were considered negative. Photographs were documented after staining.
positivity_threshold: Deep blue stains, which were local, stippled and patchy were considered to be positive, whereas faint blue stains, which were wide, shallow & could be easily washable, were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: deep blue (local, stippled, patchy) stain retention; negative: faint/washable stain
comments_index_test: This is a multi-arm study (4 index tests: VELscope, methylene blue, toluidine blue, Lugol's iodine) applied to the same 30 patients, creating non-independence between arms. Results are reported separately by lesion type (OL, OLP, OSMF — 10 patients each), which limits statistical power. The step-by-step application protocol for methylene blue (concentration used, dwell time, rinsing steps) is not described. Sensitivity and specificity calculations for the OSMF group are problematic as all 10 OSMF patients had histopathology-positive results (no true negatives), making specificity incalculable. The paper reports 100% PPV and 0% specificity for methylene blue in OSMF, indicating all histopathology cases were dysplastic in this subgroup.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the suspicious area (clinically diagnosed OL, OLP, or OSMF lesion) after VELscope examination; staining was performed on the lesion identified during clinical evaluation.
technique: Lugol's iodine (composed of iodine and potassium iodide) was applied to the suspicious oral mucosal area. The dye binds to carbohydrates and starch in tissues; normal epithelium with intact glycogen stains brown or black, while malignant/dysplastic tissues with reduced glycogen content remain unstained. Uptake of stain was considered positive for dysplasia; no uptake or light uptake was considered negative. Photographs were documented after staining.
positivity_threshold: Uptake of stain was considered as positive for dysplasia; no uptake of stain or light uptake of staining was considered as negative for dysplasia. Normal epithelium stains brown or black; malignant/dysplastic tissues with reduced glycogen remain unstained.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: absence of brown/black stain (unstained = reduced glycogen = dysplasia)
comments_index_test: Results for Lugol's iodine are reported separately by disease subgroup (OL: 10 patients; OLP: 10 patients; OSMF: 10 patients), not as a single pooled arm. For OL: sensitivity 44.4%, specificity 16.7%, PPV 100%, NPV 100%. For OLP: sensitivity 71.4%, specificity 33.3%, PPV 71.4%, NPV 33.3%. For OSMF: sensitivity 60%, specificity 0%, PPV 100%. All 30 patients received all four index tests (VELscope, toluidine blue, methylene blue, Lugol's iodine), creating a within-patient multi-arm design with potential for carry-over or ordering effects. The staining sequence is not fully specified. Meta-analysts should note the disease-subgroup-specific results and the small sample sizes (n=10 per subgroup).

site_selection_index_test: VELscope examination was applied to all suspicious oral mucosal lesions identified on conventional oral examination (COE). The examination was performed at 7 PHCs and 2 CHCs in the study area by a dental surgeon/trained field investigator.
technique: After conventional oral examination, autofluorescence examination was performed using VELscope (LED Medical Diagnostics Inc, Burnaby). Greenish fluorescence from a site was considered indicative of normal and healthy mucosa. Dark/brownish colour fluorescence observed through the VELscope was considered positive for dysplastic changes within the mucosa. Dysplastic tissues with significant keratinization (leukoplakia) could exhibit increased whiteness with loss of fluorescence (darkness) around the periphery of the lesion. Lesions were rated as malignant or dysplastic only when there was a complete fluorescence visualisation loss (FVL); lesions showing autofluorescence patterns other than complete FVL were included in the FVR group.
positivity_threshold: Dark/brownish colour fluorescence observed through VELscope was considered positive for dysplastic changes within the mucosa. Lesions were rated as malignant or dysplastic only when there was a complete FVL (fluorescence visualisation loss); lesions showing autofluorescence patterns other than a complete FVL were included in the FVR (fluorescence visualisation retained) group.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: complete fluorescence visualization loss (FVL / dark appearance)
comments_index_test: 1) Verification bias risk: biopsy site selection was guided by VELscope results — 'The biopsy sites were selected based on fluorescence loss. In case the Velscope test was negative, the site for biopsy was dictated by clinical examination.' This means all 250 lesions received biopsy regardless, but site selection was influenced by the index test, which could introduce partial verification bias. 2) Unit of analysis ambiguity: the study recruited 250 patients each with one suspicious lesion, so patients and lesions appear to be equivalent (1:1). 3) COE also evaluated as a comparator test in the same population; both tests were performed sequentially on all 250 subjects. 4) Notable that 12 cases were unclassifiable by white light examination but were still included in VELscope analysis. 5) The total malignant cases differ slightly between tables (48 in Table 3/4 vs. 49 in Table 2) — a minor inconsistency worth noting for meta-analysis.

index_test_reagent_name: Methanol-based buffered preservative (ThinPrep PreservCyt); Papanicolaou stain (ThinPrep staining reagents)
index_test_commercial_name: ThinPrep (Hologic Inc); Orcellex brush (Rovers Medical Devices)
site_selection_index_test: OLBC was applied to clinically evident oral mucosal lesions in patients presenting with OPMDs (oral leukoplakia/erythroplakia, OLP/OLL, or OSCC). The most common sampling sites were labial/buccal mucosa (34.2%), lateral surface of the tongue (27.1%), floor of the mouth (15.8%), and alveolar ridge/palate (22.9%). The Orcellex brush has a 'suitable design to easily adapt to all oral sites.'
specimen_collection: Transepithelial cells were collected from oral mucosal lesions using the Orcellex brush (Rovers Medical Devices, The Netherlands) under local anesthesia before surgical biopsy. Brush heads were immediately preserved in vials of methanol-based buffered preservative (ThinPrep PreservCyt, Hologic Inc) and transferred to a laboratory for processing.
technique: OLBC was performed using the Orcellex brush under local anesthesia prior to surgical biopsy. Brush heads were immediately preserved in ThinPrep PreservCyt methanol-based buffered preservative vials and sent to the laboratory. A liquid-based cytology slide was automatically prepared from each OLBC sample using the standard ThinPrep 2000 processor protocol (Hologic Inc). Slides were Papanicolaou stained using ThinPrep staining reagents (Hologic Inc) per manufacturer's protocol and then assessed cytologically using the modified 2014 Bethesda system. All samples were associated with pinpoint bleeding to ensure harvested cells were obtained from all epithelial layers.
positivity_threshold: LBC slides were categorized into five groups: (1) atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance; (2) atypical squamous cells suggestive of oral lichen planus or lichenoid reaction (cyto OLP/OLL); (3) low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion; (4) high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion; and (5) OSCC. For binary diagnostic comparisons, categories 3–5 (low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, OSCC) constituted positive findings for OED/OSCC, with N/C ratio thresholds: low-grade SIL ≤50%, high-grade SIL >50% and ≤75%, OSCC ≥75%.
