positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: cytological categorization as low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, or OSCC based on modified 2014 Bethesda system (5-category scale with N/C ratio thresholds)
calibration_of_assessors: Three assessors (M.I., O.K., P.S.) independently and blindly assessed all LBC slides; any discrepancy in assessment was settled by consensus. No formal pre-study calibration exercise or training sessions are described.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Yes — LBC slides were blindly assessed by three assessors, implying they were masked to histopathological results at the time of cytological evaluation.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper states slides were assessed 'blindly' but does not specify whether assessors were blinded to other clinical information such as patient history, demographics, or prior diagnoses beyond histopathological results.
comments_index_test: This is a single-arm study (one index test: OLBC). All 315 enrolled patients received OLBC immediately before surgical biopsy under local anaesthesia; 31 (9.8%) excluded for inadequate cellularity, leaving 284 for analysis. Inadequate cellularity was not statistically associated with patient age, sex, lesion site, or histopathological diagnosis. Local anaesthesia was given primarily because patients were already scheduled for surgical biopsy, potentially affecting generalisability to non-biopsy settings. One assessor (M.I.) also performed clinicopathological correlations for OLP/OLL diagnosis, raising potential for role overlap between index test and reference standard assessors. The paper references a previous 2018 study (Alsarraf et al.) using the same modified Bethesda system on a smaller cohort (101 patients) as a precursor validation study.

index_test_reagent_name: 5% acetic acid and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water), assessed via Reid's Colposcopic Index with cutoff of 5
site_selection_index_test: Colposcopy was applied to the clinically suspected oral potentially malignant disorder (OPMD) lesion presented by each patient. The lesion itself was the target of examination.
technique: The procedure was performed as follows: (1) mucosa wiped with saline; (2) green filter used to view vascular patterns at high magnification (≥×30); (3) 5% acetic acid applied to the lesion for approximately 60 seconds to assess aceto-whitening score at low magnification (≤×20); (4) Lugol's iodine solution applied to the lesion to assess iodine intake score at low magnification (≤×20). Results were scored using the Reid's Colposcopic Index (RCI) by 2 assessors independently.
positivity_threshold: The cutoff value to segregate dysplastic lesions from nondysplastic lesions was 5 according to the RCI. A score of ≥5 indicates a dysplastic lesion.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: RCI total score ≥5
calibration_of_assessors: The colposcopic score for each participant was done by 2 assessors independently; no formal pre-study calibration or training exercise is described.
comments_index_test: Both the RCI arm and the Swede scoring system arm used the same colposcopic procedure on the same 25 patients (23 analyzed); the arms are not independent — they represent two different scoring interpretations of identical colposcopic examinations. This shared-patient design means the two arms cannot be treated as independent in meta-analysis. The 2 patients missed for biopsy (1 OLP, 1 OL) were excluded from accuracy calculations, reducing the analyzable sample to 23. No sample size justification is provided. The gynecology-derived Swede 'lesion size' criterion (expressed in quadrants for cervix) was adapted for oral use by lesion dimensions (mm), which may introduce measurement inconsistency.

index_test_reagent_name: 5% acetic acid and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water), assessed via Swede Scoring System with cutoff of 8
site_selection_index_test: The colposcope was applied to the clinically identified oral lesion (OPMD) in each patient; the examination was targeted at the lesion presented by the patient seeking diagnosis.
technique: After wiping the mucosa with saline, the green filter was used to view vascular patterns at high magnification (≥×30). Then, 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion for about 60 seconds to assess aceto-whitening score at low magnification (≤×20). Then, Lugol's iodine solution was applied to the lesion to assess iodine intake score at low magnification (≤×20). Results were scored using the Swede scoring system (cutoff ≥8 = dysplastic).
positivity_threshold: Cutoff value of 8 according to the Swede scoring system to segregate dysplastic lesions from nondysplastic lesions.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: Swede score ≥8
calibration_of_assessors: Two assessors scored each case independently; no formal pre-study training or calibration procedure is described.
comments_index_test: Both index test arms (RCI and Swede Scoring System) were applied to the same 23 patients in a paired/within-patient design using an identical procedural technique; only the scoring algorithm differs. This means the two arms are not independent. Two patients were excluded from analysis due to missing biopsy (reference standard), reducing the analyzable sample from 25 to 23. No formal inter-rater reliability statistic (e.g., kappa) is reported for the two assessors, despite dual independent scoring. The 'lesion size' parameter in the Swede system has no direct cervical-to-oral adaptation, which the authors note affects specificity (low specificity for size due to OLP involving large mucosal areas).

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspicious OPMDs already identified by prior conventional oral examination. All study participants with suspicious OPMDs (detected under conventional incandescent operatory light) underwent a subsequent oral examination using the OralID® fluorescence device.
technique: The OralID® device emits a visible blue light (435–460 nm) directly into the oral cavity. The clinician views tissue fluorescence through the device. Oral lesions illuminated bright green or white-green were recorded as no OPMDs (negative). Those with lack of fluorescence or dark areas, or a combination of bright green/white green fluorescent and dark areas, were recorded as OPMDs (positive).
positivity_threshold: Those with lack of fluorescence or dark, or a combination of bright green/white green fluorescent and dark areas were recorded as OPMDs (positive).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of fluorescence (dark area) or mixed bright/dark fluorescence pattern
calibration_of_assessors: The examiner is described as 'a highly trained HIV-dental care provider' but no formal calibration or training protocol specific to the OralID® device is described.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not blinded. The same dentist performed both the conventional oral examination and the fluorescent oral examination. The paper acknowledges this 'could result in a high likelihood of report bias.' No blinding to histopathology results is described.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded. The same clinician who performed the conventional oral examination (and was therefore aware of clinical findings, patient history, and demographics) also performed the autofluorescence examination.
comments_index_test: 1) Unit of analysis is lesions (n=44), not patients — sensitivity/specificity calculations are lesion-based. 2) Verification bias risk: biopsy was only obtained for unresolved suspicious OPMDs at 15-day follow-up; spontaneously resolving lesions were diagnosed by clinical impression alone, meaning not all lesions had histopathological confirmation as the reference standard. 3) No blinding of the examiner to conventional examination findings or to clinical information — same dentist performed both tests. 4) Single HIV-specialized dental clinic; small sample; results may not be generalizable.
